"Sluzhba Bezopasnosti, eh? I've heard of guys like you. Why are you bothering an old man like me?" Pyotr asked as Dmitry approached him slowly.

"President Shukshin wants you to rally your old comrades in arms. Rally the people, cause problems for these Japs. The President aims to retake Birobidzhan and he believes that restarting the resistance will make the Japanese more open to negotiation with the Federation." Dimitri explained, finally lowering his hands.

"President Shukshin? He's so fixated on Moscow these days, didn't think the guy cared about us here in Manchuria," Pyotr wondered aloud.

He turned away from Dimitri, thinking to himself for a moment. When Russia shattered, the NAJUA and other Russian partisans had been left to fend for themselves before the Kwantung Army finally broke them in Khabarovsk. Now the President of his homeland reunited wants him to jump into the fray. But it wasn't so easy. The people were complacent after so long, the cells tiny and defeated. Pyotr lost many of his brothers and sisters in arms in their impossible mission to free the Amur basin from Japanese rule and it amounted to nothing. But that was without a strong Russia to support them. Perhaps, this time, there would finally be a chance of success. Maybe there is a chance that he could fulfill his mission: to liberate his fellow Russians. Pyotr sighed as he turned around to face Dimitri.

options.name: "We might just die for it, but we'll do it."

title: NOV_reunification.40.t
desc:
To Agent "Eagle"

As you may be aware, negotiations will begin between the Russian Federation and the Empire of Japan shortly. As it stands, many variables will be factored in Japan's decisions during these critical days. As native Russians, you are expected to fulfill your duties to rouse the spirit of our people in the region such that the Japanese strongly reconsider their position in Manchuria. In case this letter is intercepted, you will be expected to be creative in your interpretation of this order without specific instructions.

NOTICE

While these tumultuous times may inspire brazen attitudes and actions in your contingent, it must be stressed how negatively attacking civilians, even Japanese, will reflect on the Russian people. We are in delicate times, do not make mistakes which would lead diplomats to make unworthy and untrue accusations.

Your benefactor.

title: NOV_reunification.41.t
desc:
Pokryshkin sauntered towards the sleek flying machine, sunlight glinting off its polished metal wings, a proud smirk on his face. "What do you think, Vasily? It's beautiful, isn't it?" the Aviator asked. "Not corporate-made, that's for sure!" the President quipped as he followed closely behind the experienced pilot. The Federation had recently released a new batch of combat planes, and Pokryshkin would be one of the first to try them.

Alexander had a massive grin as he soared through the skies in the Federations newest generation of jet fighter: the proud MIG-23. An aircraft with enough speed and firepower to challenge the Luftwaffe in the skies.

"How's the weather up there?" Shukshin asked through Pokryhshkin's headset.

"It's fine, Vasily. Ah, I've been away from the skies for far too long!" Alexander exclaimed as he nose-dived, performing several barrel rolls before pulling back up.

"What do you think, old friend? Is it fast enough to win us the skies?"

"Vasily, with an aircraft like this, we could take over the world if we wanted!" Pokryshkin replied as he looked below the clouds to the vast plains and numerous rivers of his homeland.

He was going to make Vasily grin like an idiot when he finished this little trick. Pokryshkin pushed the engine further, even faster, until it created a powerful sound that cracked the skies.

title: NOV_reunification.42.t
desc:
Vladimir observed the recruits standing shoulder to shoulder, remaining quiet as he sized them up. The new batch wasn't much to look at, but this was to be expected with the All-Russian Army loosening its standards.

Vladimir understood why this was done. President Shukshin was on the warpath, his eyes focused on the old capital, Moscow, and the Federation would need as many troops as it could muster if they were to repel the Wehrmacht from Eastern Europe. That didn't mean he had to like training the next generation of Russian soldiers for the next few years, though.

"My name is Vladimir Orlov. You are to refer to me as either Sergeant Orlov or just Sergeant. Throughout your training, you will learn how to fire various types of weaponry, how to work together as a combat team on the ground, and how to survive on the battlefield. No matter what, you are to obey not only my orders but the orders of all your superiors during your time in this army. Do I make myself clear?"

"Yes, Sargent!" the recruits all answered in unison.

Vladimir nodded before turning to a long table that was lined with the standard-issue AV-50 rifle.

"I want each of you to take a rifle from the table and proceed to the firing range. I want to see how your aim is. Don't bother fighting over the guns. There's one for each of you, all the exact same." Vladimir ordered and the recruits obeyed, grabbing a rifle and proceeding to the firing range as instructed.

Vladimir watched them fiddle with the rifles for a moment before sighing to himself.

title: NOV_reunification.43.t
desc:
Tomsk State University!

Ever wanted to do titrations with broken flasks? Tomsk State University!

How about biology with thrice dissected frogs? Tomsk State University!

As much as Nataliya would like to keep making fun of her school, her second year was going a lot better than her first, if this dissection were any hint.

"Okay, class. Now, we begin the second part of this procedure. I understand we're all excited about the new microscopes," an old professor of biology spoke from his position at the front of the class, a cellophane sheet projector showing the instructions for a microscope cell viewing in beige and black. "But please do not go breaking the brand new equipment. Lord knows it's too new for us to start breaking - I don't think the government is that generous. Okay. Now, as we can see, the Ob river's water is quite polluted. You can see the particulates here, yes? The bacteria are normal - though quite interesting. Yes, Alexei?" he pointed to a man with his hand raised.

"Sir, I found a sort of disk-thing?"

"Come now, Alexei, you should read your textbook more often. A wonderful Protista known as an Arachnodiscus, a diatom bottom-feeder. Quite beautiful, aren't they? Anyone want to tell me something about the Arachnodiscus to the class for a bonus point on the next exam?"

Nataliya immediately raised her hand, "They have a silicified cell wall?"

"Well, Nataliya, I hadn't called on you yet, but yes, they do indeed have silicified cell walls. Now, let me look around here - these fancy sheets are so much fun to play with..."

Yes, class was getting more interesting - and more useful. Without the equipment, Nataliya wasn't sure if her biology degree would be worth anything. What kind of education were you supposed to get without hands on experience? And what do you need for hands on experience? New equipment.

title: NOV_reunification.44.t
desc:
The past few years were a struggle for Magna. His wife passed away four years ago in an industrial accident. Frankly, it seemed like no one cared. Hardly anyone came to her funeral - the parish priest, his daughters, and their nuclear families, that was it. He'd sued Feniks Infantry Solutions, but the judge censured him for filing a "frivolous lawsuit". His words. He'd had to raise his little girls alone, listening to them cry for their mama in their sleep every night. And now, he held a letter from the Chita tax office in his hands.

Truth is, he was struggling to pay the bills. Magna's job couldn't cover everything he had to pay for. His elder daughter's education, the car, food, insurance, water and gas... In fact, he'd taken to skipping meals just to keep the lights on.

"Papa? Are you okay?"

Magna looked over his shoulder. Little Yana was standing there, a worried expression on her face. He knew she was looking for a whiskey bottle in his hand. "I'm fine, little mouse. Why don't you go back outside and play with Elizabeth?" Magna mustered a weak smile, and motioned to the battered screen door.

She wandered out the door. He held his breath as he returned his attention to the letter. It was an execution order, really, not a bill. He opened it with shaking hands, braced himself, and unfolded the milk-white paper. It smelled of ink, and tears.

"Dear Mister Lebedev," he read, "in light of your distressed financial situation, the Ministry of Finance has determined that you are available for a tax refund in the amount stated below."

Wait, what?

Magda dropped the letter in shock. He looked out the window, and watched his daughters play in the leaves for a moment. Then, he put on his jacket, and opened the door to the backyard.

options.name: "Girls, get your things. We're going out for dinner!"

title: NOV_reunification.45.t
desc:
Nikita had lived in Samara all his life. The city had worn many names, ruled by Tsars, Soviets and Collaborators alike. Before the Great Patriotic War, Samara was the economic powerhouse of the Volga River, home to hundreds of billowing factories. The Luftwaffe brought those days to an end. Even when the West reunited, the city never recovered its former glory. It seemed that Samara's Golden Age was over.

But things changed when the Federation took over. Corporations moved into the city. Sibir. Titan. Feniks. Nikita got a better job in a reopened factory and sent his kids to a good school with the extra money. Entrepreneurs from as far as Magadan trekked to his hometown, opening new businesses and renovating unlivable apartments. New jobs and better accommodations halved the homeless population in four months.

Local elections were held throughout the city. Nikita didn't vote; he still remembered the days of KONR, when putting your name on the wrong ballot was a life-threatening mistake. But his neighbors who voted against the VRPP were still there the next day. Then, the next week. Then, the next month. Then, Nikita stopped counting the days, and realized President Shukshin was sincere.

Six months later, Samara was invited to elect a member of the Duma. Nikita cast his ballot for the first time in decades with a smile on his face. In the days after, he followed the tally closely, and whooped when his candidate won. He took to reading the newspaper in the park on his lunch breaks, stuffing sandwiches into his mouth as he learned about the Federation's government. The different parties, the major figures. Alexander Pokryshkin, the Flying Ace, and Vasily Shukshin, the Peasant who became President. One month, they were butting heads over industrial projects in Kazan. The next, they worked together to sponsor a Veteran's aid bill. The intricacies of Novosibirsk politics were nearly impossible to follow. But Nikita saw real debate, real disagreement, and knew this was a government he could be proud of.

options.name: The gentle breeze flowed over his face, and he smiled.

title: NOV_reunification.46.t
desc:
As a Yekaterinburg native, Vadim had grown used to the militarist culture that defined the city since the rule of Konstantin Rokossovsky. When the Federation took the city, the sudden introduction of Novosibirsk's business-centric culture-shocked him greatly. The drastic influx of entrepreneurs and managers changed Yekaterinburg nearly overnight. Soon, local elections were held, and Boris Yeltsin was elected oblast governor. They had endured countless changes; but in recent weeks, change was marching on the horizon again.

Ever since President Shukshin's speech, it seemed the entire Federation was on the warpath, its feet firmly set on the road to Moscow.

"What're you thinking about, Vadim?" Artyom, his shift manager, asked. They stood together on the production line, surrounded by the clanging of machines.

Vadim sighed, staring at the long line of rifling that filled the assembly belts. "The city feels as it did in the 40s. There was tension, the..." Vadim trailed off as flashes of tanks and screaming entered his mind. "Why is Shukshin provoking Germany again? Is he trying to condemn Russia? We've lost to the Germans twice, why would this time be different?" he said, rubbing his eyes.

Artyom placed a hand on his shoulder, a grim line on his face.

"I don't know, Vadim. But our job isn't to question why. We aren't Narodniki traitors, and our country chose this man. Now, we fight for Russia once again." he gripped Vadim's shoulders hard, "You have two choices, Artyom. You can work in this factory, do your job for Russia, or you can betray her and doom her again. Get back to work," he walked off, leaving Artyom to his thoughts as the line moved ever onwards.

title: NOV_reunification.48.t
desc:
"I'm telling you, the Reichskommisariat isn't going to last very long, we need to-" a German administrator was discussing in the conference room when a Wehrmacht officer strenuously opened the door.

"Under orders of the Führer, all officials within this building are to be moved to Germany proper. This building needs to be evacuated immediately. Security breaches and partisan movement has made this place too dangerous," the young officer demanded. The members of the conference got out of their seats and headed for the door, fear evident in their eyes. "Hurry the fuck up, Siegfried, you fat bastard, before I leave you here for some Slavic beast to blow your brains out!" the Wehrmacht officer commanded, banging his fist on the wall. "Right... apologies." Siegfried stood, but before he got on his feet, a bullet cracked through the air.

The officer laid in a pool of his blood on the floor, a bullet hole straight through the back of his skull. A raggedly dressed partisan wearing the Russian tricolour on his arm swaggered into the room, armed with a Tokarev in his hand. The door clicked, locked by the hands of another partisan outside. Dmitry lifted his pistol in the air, and his voice boomed with a smile across his face, "Right, it's time to get down to business!" Dmitry shouted, opening fire on the ceiling, before pointing it at a German bureaucrat and putting a hole between the eyes. The suited men watched in horror at their doom. Dmitry slowly approached one of them, "Y-You subhuman monster, don't touch me! I will not die by the hands of a Sla-" a bang rang out. "Who's next, eh?" Dmitry asked, a smug look on his face. One of the Germans furiously tugged on the locked door before his blood coated the handle. Slowly, the room was painted red, and Dmitry was the only one alive in the room.

He looked out the window, taking a cigarette out of his pocket and casually opened a cracked window, letting in the cloudy evening light. Idly, he flicked a speck of dried blood on his glove, "You got blood on my outfit, Kraut," Dmitry said to a corpse on the floor. "Ahh, Moskowien..." Dmitry looked over the scenery, "One day, this will all be Russia once again." He puffed a cloud of smoke into the air.

title: NOV_reunification.49.t
desc:
"You are cleared for landing, Starshina. Approach the runway, and please don't crash into it. Thing just got installed yesterday, let's not fuck it up so soon." a raspy voice crackled over the intercom. With a confident press of his thumb, Boris Pavlenko, Starshina in the VVS turned on his mic.

"Roger, roger, command. Starshina Pavlenko, making the approach. Should be a smooth landing to Onega Air Base 238. Landing, out."

Their new jet fighters and CAS systems, along with these vital airbases made the old petty officer feel like a million bucks. He'd never traveled so fast before, never cracked through the speed of sound, and in a few years, their scientific development had been astronomical. The plane felt modern, it felt like something that could actually match the German fleet. Now, they just needed the training and lift-off points. Pavlenko's landing was smooth, a beautiful touch down that glid to a stop comfortably. As he finished engaging the parking systems, he opened the hatch to let himself out. His commanding officer awaited him.

"Fan-fucking-tastic, Starshina. We're about ready to kick some Kraut ass, if all the pilots could land and fly like you. What'd you think of the new tarmac, eh?" he slapped Pavlenko on the back, his smile a mile wide.

Pavlenko took off his goggles and inspected the pristine facility. "Seems to me like we might have a bat's chance in hell of smoking the fascists. Long as this place doesn't get bombed in two minutes, that is."

No amount of anti-air systems could stop the Luftwaffe, only a comparable Russian air force could. However, with some judicious spending and a lot of crunch time... it might just turn the tide of battle.

options.name: War is more than the troops on the ground.

title: NOV_reunification.50.t
desc:
Andrei walked in front of a long row of gleaming T-72's, inspecting each tank with care. They were in good condition, more than ready for the field. "Whoever designed these was a genius," he muttered with a smile. He heard a shuffling gait, maybe some animal? He turned back to see a much older man in the uniform of the Soviet Armed Forces looking upon the tanks with curiosity in his eyes and a cane in his hand. Andrei watched him for a moment before setting his clipboard aside and approaching the old timer.

"Excuse me, sir. I don't believe I've seen you before. Do you have clearance to be here?" the young officer asked.

The older man turned to Andrei and smirked. "Oh, can't a veteran look upon the tools my young comrades will use to liberate the West?" From his chest, the distinct gold star of the Hero of the Soviet Union shone with pride.

Andrei sputtered. "My apologies, I didn't know-"

The veteran tapped one of the tanks with his cane and grinned. "If we'd had these during the Great Patriotic War, we'd have made it to Berlin in a week."

Andrei chuckled. "We've been preparing for the fight ahead. We'll be back in Moscow in no time, I can promise you that!"

The veteran smiled and put his hand on Andrei's shoulder.

title: NOV_reunification.52.t
desc:
"When the Wehrmacht stormed France and later Russia, they changed warfare forever with their revolutionary doctrine, the name of which is enough to instill fear and flashbacks to even the most hardened of veterans, blitzkrieg. But the real term, if you were to study the doctrines, is actually bewegungskrieg - the war of movement. Mechanized forces can pierce enemy defenses, outmaneuvering them and placing entrenched forces in surrounded, ruined positions. The ground forces can then mop up these encircled divisions and tear through the front lines. If we are to defeat the Germans, we need the mechanized forces capable of repelling such attacks and deal a returning blow." General Novikov explained, his eyes on the war map.

"What about our industries? Can they keep up with the demand for tanks needed to replicate this?" Shukshin asked, looking over to Kerchenko.

"Our industrial capacity has grown tremendously in recent years. I've been in contact with the heads of Feniks and Sibir. They've told me their plants are up to the task" Mikhail explained.

Vasily glanced over to Pokryshkin. The aviator had a reserved expression on his face, thinking deeply to himself. "Did you have anything to add, Alexander?" Shukshin asked, turning to his friend.

"We're really doing this," he muttered, walking over to the war map. "I fear for the future, Vasily. I'm not sure what the outcome of all this will be. But! I've learnt to put my faith in you and I don't doubt the abilities of General Novikov and Kerchenko. I like our odds, Vasily. I think we've got a chance this time around." Alexander explained, turning back to the three men in the room.

With a soft smile, Shukshin put his hand on Pokryshkin's tense shoulder.

title: Another Late Night
desc:
"Shit, I'm fucking tired," Kira muttered. "Want a coffee? I don't know if they have twenty sugars for you, but I can check." "Fuck off". John smiles tiredly before replying. "Let's try one more permutation. Then I'll see if Georgy can rustle us up some food."

"Did they feed you this well back in America?" Kira asked. She sat down on an elderly office chair next to John as he continued typing into the computer.

He scoffed.

"No, the CIA never dreamed of eating potatoes three times a day. Who knew it would be so good for my complexion," John said. "Here, I want to try another variant of the Ellis Method. This time I'm programming the computer to execute chosen-cipher text Delta with the new orientation Maxsim taught us last week". "Maxsim doesn't know shit, fucking Tomskie," Kira said. "Poor guy couldn't find his own feet if they weren't attached to him."

"Be polite, Kira Gorkoronva. At least Maxsim knows how to vote," John said. "You'd think after the shit Russia went through under the Revolutionary Front, people like you would learn not to vote for reds." He finished inputting his commands into the whirring computer and pressed the enter key. "Anyway, that'll be a few minutes."

"Another round of poker? " Kira asked. "Maybe Svetlana can loan you some money". "Oh, you think they didn't teach me how to bluff at the Company?"

Three hours passed in semi-boredom. Kira had scooped up another winning hand and John's lunch money when the computer whirred to a halt. "Shit, finally," Kira said. "I'll get it." She limped over to the computer monitor, expecting that the intercepted German message would be a garbled mess, as always.

"Oh, fuck," she said.

"What's wrong?"

"Orders from Hauptmann Wegener," she read, trembling. "Fighter Wing 107 to redeploy to Navgard Airfield by 17:00 hours."

title: The Old Man and the Sea
desc:
"I can't fucking believe it," Private Sergei Korolkov said. "I travelled all the way from Alekseevka to stare at a fucking ocean".

Sergeant Barrikad Klimov merely grunted. The old man sat, eating his sandwich, barely offering Private Korolkov his attention at all.

"You know, if the Germans do invade from the sea, we'll both be killed," Kolkov said.

"Our job is to run before they land, kid."

"I'm not a kid! I'm a man, and a soldier of the Federation army. And if those fascist dogs dare to lay a foot upon my nation's soil, I'll shoot the bastards where they stand."

Klimov shook his head. "You lied about your age when you volunteered."

"No, I didn't."

"Then tell me," Barrikad asked, "which warlord controlled West Russia before the Federation invaded?"

"Uh, Georgy Malenkov?"

Klimov shook his head. "You're so full of shit, I can smell it on your breath." Klimov turned to face Private Kolkov, sandwich dripping tomato juice into the sparse grass."When I fought for the West Siberian People's Republic, I was stationed in Zlatoust. This gang, the Aryan Brotherhood, seized Perm. A couple of months later, they started testing our borders. A raid here, a feint here, an assassination there. I was reassigned to Lysva. By the time I arrived, the Aryans had already captured the city. You know what they did?"

Private Korolkov shook his head no."They went through the city, rounded everyone up, and cut their hands off. Then left them to starve. You ever seen a two-year-old screaming for his parents with no fucking hands?"

Sergei said nothing. His stomach had already turned upside down. "The Germans did worse than that during the Great Patriotic War," Sergeant Barrikad said.

options.name: "Be thankful you won't have to see such things in your dreams."

title: The Federation Marches to War
desc:
Throughout Siberia, across the Ural mountains, from one bank of the blue Volga to the other, the Federation is awakening. Like a giant woken from a thousand years of slumber, it stirs fitfully and rises to its enormous feet with the strength of a mountain.

In Gorky and Chelyabinsk, Samara and Yekaterinburg, great forges are heated by the ignition of Russian hopes and dreams. The people of those cities work day and night, churning out hundreds if not thousands of tanks ready to charge into Saxony.

In Irkutsk and Omsk, young men kiss their sweethearts, or their wives, goodbye. They give of themselves to fulfil a duty to their nation and their loved ones, to build a world where their families can be free.

In Tyumen and Novosibirsk, veterans of air warfare and greenbacks alike take to the skies, flying practice sorties over the snowy plains of Siberia. From above, it all seems so small.

In Kamchatka and Arkhangelsk, veterans of the Red Navy set aside their politics to battle for the liberation of millions. Their only wish is that they could've won under Bukharin. They weep for those souls lost in the Second World War, and every man, woman, and child burned by the white-hot rod of slavery since those dark days began.

In Verkhneudinsk and Kazan, men not of Russia prepare to take up arms. Their sacrifices will be remembered as the greatest of all in the decades to come.

In Ukraine and the Caucasus mountains, old men dig up rifles long buried. Their units, their brothers, have been decimated four times over. The old men don't expect to live to the end of the Second West Russian War. But their roar of defiance will shake Atlas' weary arms.

In the Presidential Palace, President Shukshin waits patiently, his eyes to the west. Soon, the Federation will be going to war once more and the people will be ready for the struggle ahead.

options.name: We shall not enter Aldagautr's hall with words of fear upon our lips.

title: Doom Foretold
desc:
Danylo was pouring concrete to form the base of a communications bunker when he felt it. The sky was too wide. Too blue, too sunny. Perfect flying conditions for a German fighter. The horizon was clear, and he knew the Federation Air Force was too powerful to allow the Luftwaffe to simply waltz in and strafe him. But every time he turned his back, he could feel the bullets ripping through his skin. Wait, was that the whine of a diving aeroplane? Danylo's hands began to tremble; he felt nauseous, and weak, like he'd been deprived of food for a week. His heart pounded out of his chest, and he couldn't get enough air. Why couldn't he breathe?

Danylo doubled over, gasping. Sweat poured from his brow into his thick beard. He held out a hand to steady himself and collapsed into the dirt.

"Brother, brother, can you hear me?" Someone was slapping him."My son, can you breathe?"

"Who are you?" Danylo croaked.

"I am Father Dmitry Panin," the unknown man said. "Do you need an ambulance?"

Danylo shook his head in the affirmative. His voice was barely a whisper. "I couldn't... The sky..." His voice trailed off.

Father Panin frowned. "I understand, my son. The Luftwaffe was no kinder to the people of Gayny than your home. I see in you the same terror that afflicts all Russians. But do not despair- Christ is with you, and he will not allow his flock to come to harm."

Danylo's eyes filled with tears. "I'm afraid, Father."

Father Panin simply nodded. "I know. I am afraid, too. Let me pray for you." He placed his right hand on Danylo's forehead, wiping away the sweat and muck that crowned him. "Father Almighty, bless this man as he labors for the protection of others. Save him from the snares and temptations of Satan, and shield his back from all wounds and iniquities. Make your presence known to him, that he may be comforted by your love."

"Saint Dymphna, great wonder-worker in every affliction of mind, I humbly implore your intercession with Jesus through Mary, in this man's hour of need. Do not leave his side!" In the distance, the whine of the ambulance grew ever closer.

title: A Black Siberia
desc:
Where there was loyalty to the League's principals, there was always treachery, and the Captain always had a nose for treachery. Dancing from corner to corner, the penned executioner finally found his next target for “questioning”. Standing idly by next to the ill-appropriate light afforded by the rusted lamppost, reading his paper in the company of none.

“Comrade citizen,” he bellowed out to the younger man. “Would you lend me a minute of your time?”

“O-Oh, uh, Comrade" the Man began. “I r-really should be off to work. Got lost in the pages as they say, right?”

“Nonsense!” Captain Dyatlov waved his gloved hand. "I insist.."

Slowly the Captain approached, placing his cuff on the young man's shoulder. Dyatlov let a grin creep upon his face, the fear was palpable.

“What’s your name, Comrade?”

“It’s V-Viktor, Viktor Semyonov."

"Well then, Viktor! You are glad I came across you. I.. consider myself more lenient than others. We can talk for a bit, maybe chat about this fine paper in your possession."

“S-Sir, I'm a-afraid if I don't get going soon, the Store's going to ope-"

"Say Semyonov, where do you work? I don't blame you for taking your time. Can't see much in this fog, you can get lost without keeping track." the Captain bored his gaze into the young man's frightened eyes, directing them to the pavement below.

"A-Anastasia's Books, just off Molokova Street."

"Is that so? And what kind of books do you sell at such an establishment?"

"U-Uh, well, I guess all kinds. Childrens, History, Philosophy. We sell whatever w-we can find, really. I work the counter and the children seem to l-love it."

Dyatlov paused for a moment, letting his artificial grin slowly turn into a face of stone.

“Well, off you go, Viktor Semyonov. I hope your work finds you well in your future endeavors."n
"O-Of course, Sir. Glory to Russia!" the man quickly scurried off into the boundless smog, leaving the Captain alone in the light.

Dyatlov reached his glove into his breast pocket, removing a small black booklet from its confines. He flipped past hundreds of identical columns before stopping on a single blank box.

options.name: Suspect 51: Viktor Semyonov. Suspected of spreading subversive literature to palatable youth. Appropriate Action: Immediate Disposal.

title: An Atmosphere Of Silence
desc:
Maxim had sat at his desk rhythmically assembling the slides of the several rifles he was ordered to make. For the past week he had been biting his tongue, the quota had been extended and now he worked through the night. He had already been making the allotted amount of weapons parts, hell he even made more most days.

“Tima what is this shit, we’ve been making the parts and now they do this to us?”

Tima quickly muttered, “Maks stop this, don’t you remember Vitya, do you want to get shot?”

Before Maxim could respond Tima walked away to ‘get parts’. Annoyed, Maxim went back to assembling slides, hearing the crunch of a League soldier on the catwalk. In fear, he quickly returned to making slides, his adrenaline-riddled hands forming several slides at once.

Before long, Tima came back and glared at his weapon parts muttering a few comprehensible words under his breath. Before long the loudspeaker croaked its awful song, “Factory Worker 4673 enter the nearest office, Worker 4673.” Inevitably the speaker stopped and quietly beset the factory. What used to be the eyes of his coworkers, whom he’d share occasional small talk with turned into dark coals. The Factory had gone silent as the ringing in his ears prevailed and he stood up, his legs aching after each stride.

The door to the office was heavy, groaning as he pushed it open. Inside this simple room stood two Black League soldiers and an officer, who welcomed him in. After sitting in silence for what felt like hours the officer finally spoke,

“What is your name worker?”

Maxim cleared his throat and muttered,

“Maxim Larionovich sir, but my friends call me Maks.”

“So you make the slides of rifles Maxim?”, the officer retorted back. Before he answered Maxim noticed a glint in the officer's eyes, a degree of morbid sadism spreading to his lips.

“Yes sir, I make the slides primarily of rifles but I can also make other weapons parts.” Maxim had replied.

In a few swift swipes, the officer crossed multiple boxes on a document, before staring at Maxim.

“Thank you for your cooperation Worker 4673.” The officer then grabbed his pistol and waved goodbye to Maxim, pulling the trigger.

options.name: They shall not corrupt our works...

title: Teach Them Hate
desc:
Ivano sat in his classroom although the last time he did so was many many years ago. There was no sweet teacher who taught everyone with a grace about basic topics such as Russian, Mathematics, and the small world around them. It was replaced with a grizzled and aged man, his face bearing a large scar down towards the tip of his nose and nearing his eye a glass one replaced what once was his own.

After sitting down the teacher introduced himself as Lazar and pulling down a clean map had shown all of Russian territory they had and with some additions, pointing westwards Lazar explained that Russia had been raped and pillaged by the Germans so much that even some of the Russian people had began to join the rank and file of the German army. 

Hearing this, and well seeing this horrified Ivano. He had heard stories from the west of some of the atrocities occurring in Western Russia. But if what he heard was true then what else had the Germans done?

Lazar, aware he shook the throng of civilians, continued to list depressing statistic after depressing statistic almost demoralizing them to the point of depression. Before ending he decided to give the people something to hate.

“What is it we can do?” one woman exclaimed.

“You can work harder, longer, and help us fight the teutonic menace with all the patriotic zeal you can muster!” Lazar responded.

title: A Slight Divergence
desc:
Yekaterina was in the middle of her work. She was checking papers in the central bureau where the most important documents about everything from military operations to propaganda campaigns to rally the population. All of that she had been entrusted to take care of. It was quite surprising considering her gender, and in spite of both dangerously low wages and the misogyny she experienced, she liked her job.

As she searches through the files detailing political prisoners, it seems that there are files that detail the location of political prisoners are missing. She checks multiple times before concluding that it is unnecessary. There had been multiple times before that documents were organized improperly, however that was just for pretty simple ones, these ones were in one of the deepest parts of the bureau. It was a discrepancy she never before had seen, while she wasn’t that worried, it still was strange.

She rose and walked to her office table where she wrote down that five files had disappeared. Right as she wrote it down she started to contemplate if it really was a good idea to note it down or not. When there had been a rare inconsistency before, she had always been yelled at by the boss, even if it was never her fault. Her male colleagues were only occasionally yelled at by the boss, even if it was the exact same discrepancy found. She continued to write, she slowly became more and more nervous. Finally she erased it. It was no big deal, right. As she slowly took a deep sigh of relief, she walked back to her work, continuing with searching through the files.

title: Some Never Grow Old
desc:
The Family Petrova may have been an ordinary family in the Soviet Union, this is however not the case after the Great Patriotic War and the arrival of the Black League. The family was split up after the Great Patriotic War and now can rarely send letters, only through secret contacts through Kazakhstan can they get their letters to Muscovy.

Elyna Petrova was doing her usual business taking care of the house. She couldn’t take her mind off the letter she got four months ago. Her husband trapped in Muscovy had gotten a job as a soldier in the Moskowien Wehrmacht and he would soon be able to reunite with her. She sent a reply immediately as she explained her concern about the Black League discovering her ties with a collaborator. Usually a response would take about four to six weeks. She hadn’t gotten a response in five months. She had grown to be strong, even after being driven away from her husband. In the early days she would cry herself to sleep every night. Now she was ready to fight against anything coming in her way, including the rigid Black League.

The doorbell rang, it rang across the small apartment. Someone coming to their house was something very unusual. She quickly walked towards the front door. She opened the door to see five policemen, all with uniforms black as the night. The head officer started speaking.

“Mrs Petrova, I am afraid we are going to have to arrest you for subversive actions against the All-Russian Black League and for having contacts with Collaborators.”

“WHAT!?! YOU CAN’T-”

The Officers proceeded to turn the apartment upside down and arrested the rest of her family left in Russia, her Mother, Father and son... They were put into the trucks of the officers. They were driven away and forgotten to history.

options.name: Another family removed so that the Great Trial can prevail.

title: The Gears Grind On
desc:
As all Black League personnel are subject to the highest standards of fitness, Glakoverkh Yazov was ordered on this date by BLP-DR-078431 (AMOSOV, Nikolai Mikhailovich) to desist from his duties and report for a complete physical and mental examination. During this period, leadership of the Black League was devolved from Yazov to Evgeniy Savintsev; duties of the Glakoverkh were divided between the leadership cadres as outlined in Succession Document 178.

Evgeniy Savintsev began the day as he did every other, with a steaming cup of black coffee and two hundred push ups. From 06:30 to 09:30, he reviewed the names of five hundred criminals, dissidents, and malformed individuals sentenced to the Redemptionary Brigades. He assigned two hundred and thirty seven to rebuild the highway between Irkutsk and Krasnoyarsk, and one hundred and twelve to mine clearing duties on the Moscowien-Russian border. The remainder were shipped to Vorkuta, to assist in Black League training operations. At 10:15, he left his desk for a three mile run with Foreign Minister Aleksandr Sakharovsky, wherein they agreed to conduct an assassination of several pro-democracy advocates in Romania.

At 11:45, Aleksandr Sakharovsky met with several members of the “Foreign Ministry'', to discuss the issue of Turkmenistan. Central Asia, as the borderlands of the Russian National Reclamation Government, occupied an increasingly large place in Sakharovsky’s mind; it is a place of dissent, of weakness, of degeneracy and anti-Black League thinking, infested by Bolsheviks and fascists alike. Eventually, a junior member of the cadre offered a suggestion that caught Aleksandr’s eye: a mass resettlement of vetted, loyal Russian populations into the largest cities of Central Asia, and a temporary displacement of unvetted Turkish and Khazak populations from the region.

At 14:20, Sakharovsky gathered with Evgeny Pitovranov and the leadership of the Economic Ministry to discuss ongoing preparations for the Great Trial. Pitovranov has repeatedly requested additional labor resources to complete fortifications on the Nowa Polska-Moscowien border, but has been rebuffed several times by both Yazov and Savintsev. Together, Sakharovsky and Pitovranov draft a proposal to mobilize the Redemptionary Brigades in low priority industries,  freeing trustworthy laborers to shift to building forts, pillboxes, and life saving defenses.

At 18:00, Pitovranov and Yuri Drozdov spoke over dinner concerning a wave of sabotages in Central Siberia. Drozdov suspects remnants of the Siberian Black Army; Pitovranov surmises the presence of German agents. They agree only that security must be doubled. Together, they compose a plan to make Novosibirsk a closed city, expelling all women, children, and unvetted civilians and permitting only trustworthy laborers to stay. Soon, this plan will extend to all major industrial hubs throughout the Reclamation Government. The traitors and the saboteurs will have nowhere to hide.

At 24:00, Glakoverkh Yazov returned from the examinations. His desk was empty, for once. He marched to his chambers, removed his shoes, and slept without worry.

options.name: Leadership entails creating new leaders, not followers.

title: The Costs Of Victory
desc:
The unification of Russia had brought something into Dimitry Yazovs life that he’d only fakely expressed to his subordinates. For once, he could now truly say without a doubt that he now possessed a sense of certainty. He could now be fully confident in the Leagues strength, and he would now truly be at the helm of his peoples destiny. But, there were issues at hand that needed to be taken care of. After all, he couldn’t simply run head first into the lands of the Aryan.

The assembly assembled before him had been assigned to hammer out a solution to every problem the League is facing or could face in the coming months. Lasting long into the night, it became clear that there were indeed several issues that had to be resolved, lest the League's chance for success in the coming Trial be at risk.

The most discussed topics included the problem of production capability, access to resources, and technological advantages that their enemy held. There were ways to solve such issues of course, but it became clear to the assembly that implementation of reforms would be severely hampered by the current economic capability of the League.

Yazov felt a burning sensation in the back of his head upon hearing those last words, and stood up to speak, immediately silencing everyone present.

“I think you’re all forgetting a core part of what made our state triumphant in unifying the Motherland. When we marched onward to reunify Russia, we did not do so only because we had such things as advantages in production capability or overwhelming firepower.”

All eyes were on Yazov now, as each man began to squirm uncomfortably in their seats.

“We triumphed because of our will, and unwillingness to ever give up on our peoples right to see the day when vengeance could be achieved in full. Yet you sit here and tell me that our will is no longer enough to solve the current issues at hand?”

options.name: “We will immediately move to implementation, sir.”

title: Name, Age, And Place Of Birth
desc:
“Next.”

Checkpoint officer Vasily Smirnov rubbed his temples with his thumbs while the next feckless idiot shuffled up to the booth.

“Name, age and place of birth.”

“Well, uh, it’s Ivanov,” the small, beetle-shaped man mumbled, “Ivan Ivanovich, that is.”

“You taking the piss?”

“Of course not, comrade checkpoint officer.”

“Hand over your papers,” Smirnov groaned, “I trust you have them on you.”

Ivan Ivanov winced as he passed a single passport beneath the glass. Smirnov sighed when he saw the hammer and sickle on the front cover.

“This look like the Soviet Union to you, Ivanov?”

“Well, its the most current—

“Most current?” Smirnov laughed, “Trust me, Ivanov, if you want to fool somebody, don’t act so fucking daft.”

“It says here, comrade sir, I was born in Sverdlovsk.”

“You don’t expect me to read this shit, do you Ivanov? Are you delusional?”

For a moment, Ivanov looked ready to burst into tears as he shuffled nervously. Just as Smirnov thought he was about to walk away, he spoke again.

“That lady that just passed through, she’s—

“Your wife? I’ve heard it all before Ivanov. I don’t give a fuck if its true or not, it comes down to this: if you can’t show me anything printed this decade, you’re not getting in. Understand?”

“Well, I have this.”

Smirnov felt his hairs stand up and his smile drop as Ivanov passed through a crisp slip of paper with a black swastika stamped on top. He examined it for a moment before speaking again.

“Ivan Ivanovich, you are a citizen of the German Reich?”

“Moskowien, to be precise, but yes.”

“And why are you attempting to enter Russia?”

“To escape,” Ivanov stared at him blankly, as if it were obvious, “to reunite with my family.”

“Ivan Ivanovich, are you aware that this document is tantamount to treason against Russia, and undeniable proof of collaboration with the German occupiers?”

“Treason?” Ivanov paled, “That can’t be true. I’ve never collaborated. How could I have?”

“Well, Ivan Ivanovich,” Smirnov reached over to the telephone, “That’s for us to find out.”

Smirnov put the telephone to his ears and waited for the tone. When he heard the grunt of the man on the other end, he spoke.

“Yes, this is Smirnov at point D, I’m gonna need a hand or two. No, nothing dangerous, just a collaborator. Oh, and his wife may have gotten through, one, uh, Maria Ivanova. I’d advise liquidation upon sight. She’s not likely to know anything.”

title: For all to see
desc:
Was it a dream? Elias wasn’t sure what had just happened. Ever since the Russians had come and thrown everyone into the old ghettoes, hunger had gnawed at his stomach without end. Some of the other kids had taught Elias to drink as much water as he could, to trick his stomach into being full. Elias thought it worked, but deep down he knew that in the end it was only a trick. The grown-ups knew it too, and so they sent the children out every morning to beg the guards for some food. Usually, the guards would just scream and kick at them until they ran away. But today, when nobody was looking, the old man with the kind eyes had leaned down and reached through the barbed wire and passed Elias a backpack, filled with bread.

Elias hurtled down the streets of the ghetto with the bag strapped to his back. He felt the eyes of starving Germans and Russian guards on him as he bolted, but he wouldn’t stop until he made it home. With every step, the bag seemed to become heavier and heavier, like it was filled with bricks. Even when it was so heavy that he felt like his back was on fire, Elias refused to slow down. His house was just around the corner.

When he burst into his home, he saw Papa and Opa, but they were not alone. About twelve other men were crowded around the kitchen table, studying a map that was spread across the surface. Red arrows and crosses had been drawn all over it, and Elias thought he even saw some rifles in the corner of the room. Before he could understand what was happening, he collapsed from the effort he had just spent. As Papa rushed over to him, a few of the other men cheered to see the bread overflowing from his bag. Elias smiled weakly as they sung and danced and Papa ran his hand over his head.

In an instant, the world turned white. Elias tried to ask what was happening, but his mouth was empty and his ears were full. When he tried to scream, his mouth filled with ash and blood. He didn’t have long to think, before a force stronger than anything he could imagine pressed down on his chest. Just as quickly, the fabric of the world seemed to rip, and a sea of blackness came rushing through the gaping chasm.

When the smoke had cleared and the ash had settled, a messaged had been scrawled across the ruined building in hateful black paint.

options.name: Know your fate. Resistance is hopeless.

title: We Are Ready
desc:
The door slammed shut, and silence returned to the bunker that served as Dmitiry Yazov’s quarters. Yazov and his staff had concluded yet another meeting, with the main talking points being on the current status of readiness for the Leagues troops and reports on the morale of the people. Dozens of files containing dizzying amounts of data had been laid out on the table before him, and Yazov had slowly combed through each and every one. When the meeting concluded, his outward persona completely changed, going from the cold, iron hearted man that the world knew, to a man shakily taking off his cap and taking several swigs of vodka.

So much work had been done. So many production facilities were created, dissidents crushed, military units trained and organized, and so much more that Yazov had begun to start wishing that the day would come sooner. The day when he would give that order, and it could begin. The day the Motherland’s redemption would finally be achieved when The Great Trial was commenced. But at the advice of his staff, he’d delayed that order so that Russia could well and truly be prepared for The Great Trial.

And now, after so long, that day was on the horizon. Finally, he thought. Finally, it would all be worth it. Every moment of progress, gained in blood since the day his mentor had given him the mantle of leading the Leagues destiny, would all be worth it. When the day came where Russian flags flew over Germania, and the Aryan was obliterated by Russian arms... finally, justice for innumerable crimes against his people would be achieved at last.

Yazov sighed, rising from his seat and reaching for his hat as he remembered once more that there were still a few remaining tasks at hand that needed to be addressed before all of his thoughts could come to fruition. He exited his room, and made his way over to the broadcasting station as he prepared himself for one last grand speech to his people before destiny.

title: All for One
desc:
Just days ago, Yegor was supposed to be fighting Teutons. Instead he busied himself with hoofing it the other direction, opposite the frontline, in the dead of night, with some extra supplies he “borrowed” for his journey. Deserting didn’t mean anything to him. He was an only child, and the only one taking care of his parents when they got grey and old. He couldn’t stand to think of how they were just barely surviving without him so he ran. He had considered the thought they might come for his family after he deserted, so he needed to just get home and get them the hell out of Russia.

Finally, he saw his village on the horizon, standing atop the hill as it always has. Yet, with all the men conscripted and gone, it seemed dead and grim. He rushed up the hill, past the market, and all the way down to the other edge of the village; the only people around to observe him were elderly women and the youngest of children.

He entered the home where he grew up and took a few more steps, into the old familiar living room, finding his mother sitting on the couch, staring ahead with eyes dead and energy completely depleted. She looked almost 10 years older, and didn’t even acknowledge Yegor as he came in.

“Mother, you’re here! We need to go, I need to get you and father out of here. Where is he? I’ll go fetch him while you pack-”

“They took him.” She replied, without a trace of emotion in her voice. She would have cried, had she any tears left.

“B-because of me...?” Yegor asked, dread running throughout his nerves.

“No. They just needed him. Gave him a uniform, a gun, everything. Told him he’s going west.” She said, finally daring to look her son in the eyes.

Yegor’s heart sank. These monsters didn’t even care that he had deserted, they just needed everyone, even an elderly man at the end of his life. He knew the conditions out there, on the front; it is no place for old men.

Yegor sat down next to his mother as he wrapped his arms around her and held her close, both of them staring into nothingness as thoughts better left unvoiced ran through their heads.

title: The Truth in the Numbers
desc:
Abrasha sat in a dark room, with the cold embrace of his metal chair and table being the only outside stimuli to keep him from outright sleeping right then and there. Today, he’d been ordered to come in and work on “A new set of data” for him to process and organize. Truth be told, he would take anything new as a blessing.

He’d spent months chipping away at the same old administrative paperwork, after having been reassigned from his beloved home of Tomsk to the depressing and minimalistic city that the League called a capital. Despite the food rationing and lack of anything resembling goods for a middle class, Abrasha’s main issue was simply boredom.

But now perhaps Abrasha could get something new. Maybe it would even put the skills he’d gained in university to use. And as he read through and examined each folder given to him, he displayed a barely noticeable smile. His wish had come true, and he tried to savor the moment as much as he possibly could in times where happiness could be considered its own luxury.

He’d been assigned to the task of looking over and diagnosing the health of the economy, and had been given access to several classified League files to accomplish this task. Abrasha thought to himself that perhaps an increase in responsibilities was on the horizon.

Eleven hours later, the once tidy looking man in uniform was now an out of control mess, with sweat dripping down his face as the temperature had gotten to a point where he had thrown his jacket to the floor. On that floor now lay countless papers and charts, painting a terrifying picture that only those with the proper knowledge could decrypt.

He slowly sank to a sitting position, sliding down the wall as he did so. Abrasha now truly understood it all. Russia no longer had an economy. In its place an engine had been constructed. That engine used the scraps of what was once prosperity to fuel a complete and total war without any chance of returning to normalcy after. Only now could he truly understand where Russia was heading, swallowed whole into the dark abyss of hatred.

options.name: “What have they done to the motherland?”

title: On Minefields
desc:
“There are no minefields in Russia and they were told to keep it that way.

Officially, the Black League espouses the need for prisoners of war to 'tame the motherland' by fertilizing the soil for farms, flattening the earth for infrastructure and urban development as well digging holes with which to bury the dead and further fortify the state.

Truth was that Leonid and his group of young prisoners had the unenviable task of clearing the land of mines that the several russian warlords had laid all throughout their motherland. Sometimes it was as easy as following the map that detailed the minefield. Other times it was as hard as finding needles in a haystack.

Clearing the mines was made harder by the fact that each of them had been given selective treatment depending on which warlord they served along with what other 'war crimes' they may have committed. If they had served a naive but benevolent warlord on top of being a 'good servant of the motherland', then they were allowed tools and a single slice of bread a day. Being the opposite meant having nothing or being executed by minefield.

He hoped that one day he and his fellow prisoner would be free men. But until the last of the teutons are dead and until justice has been served, they shall never be free."[Change Later]

title: The Men On The Front
desc:
Late into yet another Siberian night, Andrei reclined back in his chair with a newspaper and vodka in each of his hands, having missed the chance to read it earlier in the day. In large, bold letters, the headline read, “GERMANY THREATENS NUCLEAR WAR”. At the bottom corner of that same page was a public service announcement from the government, informing the public of how those first allowed into the National Redoubt System would be members of the army and their families, followed by the general populace.

Andrei himself had a mixture of emotions swirling through his head. On one hand, he, his wife, and children were guaranteed a spot after having been working in the League's governmental apparatus since before the Reunification Wars. But, besides the potential for the very collapse of humanity itself, Andrei pondered the fate of the millions of his Russian comrades who wouldn’t make it into the bunkers. Would they just be tossed aside? Discarded as though they were only a means to an end? The conclusion of that last thought was enough to convince Andrei that he needed to just go to bed, simply forget these thoughts and return to work at the recruitment office without such things to ponder.

The next morning brought something he’d never seen before. Usually, a recruitment office is almost always empty, and with little activity in it, and Andrei had worked in this building for over a decade, and his team never had an amount of enlistment requests that came close to challenging.

But that morning when he went to open the doors to the building, he saw a line of people that had to have been miles long. Andrei saw the terrified faces of tens of thousands, no doubt having read the same words and had the same thoughts he had the night before.

That day, Andrei helped thousands of families obtain spots in the bunkers, with ever more pleading and begging to have their fathers and husbands enlist so that they too may avoid the worst fate imaginable. Yet, as more and more pleaded and begged to enlist, Andrei knew he could only save so many before the military blocked any further enlistment.

options.name: Vengeance demands the highest of prices.

title: A Pain Beyond Pain
desc:
Major Friedrich Schäfer sat, handcuffed to a chair, beaten and bloodied. Dozens of cuts oozed across his body. They'd torn out his fingernails on the third day, and blood stained his once pristine uniform. The interrogation room was ice cold, every surface formed of featureless grey brick. The only sound was the humming of the lights over head.

The door to his prison slammed open, and struck the wall with a bang. Two men of the Black League, both part of the reborn interrogation cadres, shuffled inside. Behind them, a new man took the stage.

He was tall, so tall that he had to duck beneath the lip of the door. He was bald, and wore a white lab coat. His arms were inhumanely long, stretched thin like taffy, and a syringe of amber liquid sloshed in his black-gloved hands. "Ah, here is the patient." One of the interrogators offered him a stool next to Schäfer's immobilized body. "Thank you for your patience," the doctor said, smiling. He took the offered seat. "I do hope my friends have not been too brutal to you. Sometimes, I think they act in such a manner because they're simply bored." His smile dimmed. "Or perhaps they saw what happened in Smolensk."

Friedrich spat a foul mixture of blood and spit at the doctor's face. "Kill me now, untermensch. I will tell you nothing."

"That is your choice, my friend. But, I would like to test that hypothesis." The doctor gripped Schäfer's arm, and pierced the closest of his bulging veins without another word. The amber medicine poured into his body in seconds.

Every nerve in the Major's body ignited. He seized, foam bubbling in his mouth as he threw himself back and forth, unable to control his own movements. The legs of his chair slipped from the ground. Friedrich screamed as his skull cracked against the concrete floor. His lungs strained, and his heart felt as though it was soon to burst. "Please!" he screamed, "I'll talk! I'll talk!"

"No, my friend," the doctor said.

options.name: [Change Later]"I'm getting wonderful data from this."[Change Later]

title: Free Loaders
desc:
[Change Later]"Please! It's not for us, it's just for the baby! Pleeease!

Yuri's hands tightened around the rough kitchen counter, growing whiter with every cry of desperation from his sobbing wife. A whole year they had been 'living' in this soulless concrete shell. A year since they had had every family photo, every rug and ring, every ounce of color mercilessly stripped from them, sent into the belly of the foul factories. A year he had been forced to feed them, put screw upon miserable screw into radios he could never play, first aid kits he could never use.

"Pleeeeeease! Just take half! Leave us with some! Our baby is all we have!"

But they had kept going, like reeds floating in rapids, trying their damndest not to snap. And it had paid off. The miracle of life. The League could not snuff out the joy that a parent felt as a child, their child, grew. But they were trying their best. For the crime of possessing some simple wooden blocks and and some meager rations, they had sent two of the League's lackeys; a snivelly but ferocious boy, his hat too big for his head, and a towering giant of a man, his eyes two sharpened daggers. A duo as comical as it was terrifying.

But Yuri didn't care. This would be his stand. The knife in the drawer beneath his hand was bent and blunted, but it stabbed all the same. He would show everyone what good Russian people did to those who crossed the line. He'd wipe that stupid smug face off this baron in black. He would -

Angela crumpled to the floor, her arms clutching her bloodied and mutilated belly, her face now a reflection of Yuri's soul: pale and panic-stricken.

"There! Now you really don't need these little blocks and extra calories."

With a pleased smile, the two devils in uniform exited through the door, the baron giving Yuri one more crushing glare. A glare of pity, as if he was a fool to think he had ever had any control of the situation. A glare of victory.

And then the room was silent again. The frantic cries of Angela, replaced by quiet, uncanny sobs. The rage that had filled Yuri's soul, now crushed, ground into dust, and scattered before the cold midnight wind. And the beating heart of his unborn child, silenced. They would now never gaze upon all the colors and lights and sounds and smells of the world.

But perhaps that was for the best.

options.name: For the reclamation of Russia, no sacrifice is too great.

title: Separate the Wheat from the Chaff
desc:
A knock rang out from a humble house on the outskirts of Barnaul, a major grain producing area within the [OMS.GetName]. A rude awakening was to await its owner, who was ready to sell his grain the next day.

"Comrade Nikita, your grain has been deemed unsuitable for the general populace. It is too expensive and decadent for the people of the Great Trial."

Nikita shook life a leaf; this nameless official had condemned his harvest, and therefore his life. Panicking, Nikita cried out. "B-but you can’t do that, that's the entire stockpile for the year! How am I supposed to buy rations from the storage? I'll starve! You aren't so cruel, are you?"

Nikita stared at the officer, hoping that just this once, the Spartan discipline of the Black League would be relaxed for him, just this once. The officer's eyes wavered a tiny bit. Maybe they'd give him the standard pricing, even if they didn't agree to his asked prices. How dare they, anyhow? After the Union collapsed, he built his own way, he made his estate in Barnaul!

The officer slowly shook his head, "Sir, one farmer's life doesn’t matter in the grand scheme of the nation. If you starve, you shall be replaced with another, more capable person. We will begin the confiscation of this improper yield. Please vacate the field, or you will be arrested for treason."

The officer shook his head, looking away from the grim situation. For a moment, he faltered. His mind thought of traitorous things. What right did they have to kill this man for a mistake? They could just call it mass-produced, it'd be a simple response for a simple mistake. What was the point in a government to reclaim Russia if they were going to destroy their own people?

His train of thought was rudely interrupted by farmer Nikita, now on his knees, crying and begging for another chance. "I'll plant the crops, it doesn't matter to me! Just enough to live!" The last thing the officer said in the confrontation was a simple, harsh...

title: More For The Soldiers
desc:
Even through some of the harshest training programs that existed in the world, not once had Mizenov ever felt like the League had not given him enough. Meals, a roof over his head, and even a degree of respect he hadn’t ever been given before in his life were some of the things that enlisting in the military had helped him obtain.

And it didn’t stop there. Many of the civilian encounters he had often ended in a salute for his eventual service in The Great Trial, or an acknowledgement of his bravery. It had always made him even more proud to be a part of the cause, yet something always seemed a little lost in their eyes.

Mizenov never quite knew why. At least until his unit passed by the village of his childhood.

As his transport vehicle bumped along the road, he turned his gaze to the buildings he used to sleep under as a child. Although he remembered the structures never being in the best of shape, they certainly never reached the state they were in now. Pieces of brick were missing all throughout it, with many of the windows being boarded over.

And it was then that he saw the occupants of the village. Each and every one looked as though they hadn’t been fed in at least a week, with plenty of bones remaining visible. Upon their faces sat the looks of despair that Mizenov hadn’t seen since the days of the terror bombings, in some cases some even looked to have drifted into an even darker place...

The sight of his fellow Russians in such a state almost brought tears to his eyes, as this scene repeated again and again as the convoy passed through even more of the countryside. Village after village, turning men and women into fuel for the engine of war. It was the only time in his life where the seeds of doubt grew into a deep, underlying anger at the League. Perhaps, he thought, that maybe Russia had a deeper, much darker enemy than the Aryan.

options.name: “The price for vengeance is never too high.”

title: The Men in the Factories
desc:
“Listen up!”

A certainly strange awakening, unlike the usual inhumane conditions they usually live in. Dominik was certain that it wouldn’t be much more special than another word about increased quotas or a small promotion, it had never been special before, why would it today. At the factory in Barnaul, there was always a collective pessimism between the workers. They all knew that they would all one day fall to the cold embrace of death, they weren’t scared of it, the present couldn’t be much more different from it.

“Under the commandment of the central command of the All-Russian Black League, we will teach you how to survive a nuclear fallout which the Teutonic menace might one day wreak upon us. The closest fallout shelter lies to the room left of us, near the offices. If the sound of sirens rings out, please try to get to the shelter as soon as possible. If you are not quick enough, or you don’t have the time to get to your local fallout shelter, please stay calm and go as deep as you can in your building. Any other information will be detailed in the pamphlet you will receive, thank you.”

The soldiers around the officer handed out a pamphlet to every worker in the building. On the paper there were pictures showing a step by step guide on how to survive the nukes from the teutons. Dominik was surprised that they could be so compassionate, or perhaps they just wanted to have their cheap labor survive. In any case, it was a feeble attempt at giving the people hope. He doubted if most would even try to survive, he could try to, but would it be a happier life in a dead world. From the small things he had heard about this foreign ‘nuke’, it didn’t sound very pleasant to live in a world where it destroyed the world.

options.name: He lost the small hope they tried to give him.

title: Expand the Bunkers West
desc:
The deep rumbling of cement mixers and the roar of truck engines awoke Vadim from his short sleep. It had only been a week or so since the league had occupied his village, and he had sure as hell not enjoyed it. Starting at 6 o’clock every morning they would start construction around the hills surrounding the settlement, and stop around nine in the afternoon.  Working on what? He had absolutely no idea. The elders had gathered the community upon the arrival of the workers, instructing them to stay away and avoid the workers and the sites at all costs.

He was sick to death of them. Not a single night’s good sleep was had since those bastards had arrived! It was time to do something about it, even if there were some damn consequences. Leaving his house, making his way through the town square and hiking up the steep hill towards the main site, before moving through the bushes, peering into the scene below.

There were about 20 of them, the majority seeming to be workers of sorts. Looking starved and haggled, they were either lined up towards the officers inspecting them or slaving away at a large pit in the centre. Digging yet deeper into the earth, as they began lifting heavy concrete slabs and steel doors into the pit, Vadim only grew more puzzled. What just was going on here? The nearest town worth anything was Syktyvkar, and that was hundreds of miles away. What did his place matter? And what were they building? A shelter of sorts, maybe even a bunk-

He met the gaze of the officer staring at him, screaming while pointing directly at his face. There was no time to hear the shouts and orders they would give him if he stuck around another second. He just knew he had to run as fast as god would let him.

Dashing into his village, He caught his breath and started to make his way home and prayed they wouldn’t recognize him again.

title: Dig Deeper
desc:
At a table sat a group of engineers and architects, rolling out several schematics and plans that were to be the main talking point of this hastily assembled meeting. They were ordered by the League to gather together once more to discuss an extension of the same bunkers that they had all spent so much work on. Not that they could complain or say no to such an order, but it frustrated them all nonetheless.

Most frustrated of all was the designated leader of the group, Kolya, who quickly began to realize that a previously mildly aggravating situation had just developed into an unbelievably painful one, as it became clear to all present that such a request related to the expansion of underground bunker sites would require materials that their superiors simply did not have possession of.

They would need to find an alternative. Something cheaper, and in vast amounts so as to supply other sites with the means to pursue their own expansion operations if need be.

Then, they had it: Steel. It only had to be layered twice as thick as lead to get the same effectiveness, and it was 3 times as cheap. And if constructed in a fashion where the maximum amount of dirt possible could be in between the steel lining and potential radioactive fallout, the occupants of the bunker would be relatively safe.

But, the issue of effective air filtration would arise, as those too needed design changes according to the orders of the League.

Kolya and the group pondered this for a while, as they wondered how they could possibly downgrade air filtration without harming the occupants in the process. But they had to come to an answer at some point, and that involved simply hoping and praying that a few experimental methods would be enough.

But of course, they couldn’t tell their benefactors this, as the consequence for implementing plans with such blatant logical holes in them would be severe. So, with smiles and neutral faces, they later informed the council assigned to oversee them of their “successful discovery” of new design methods.

title: More Ears on the Border
desc:
It was supposed to be his off day, Braun thought as he rode by car back to his forward base near the Russian border. Torrential rains hammered on his car's windows. For some reason, the Generalfeldmarschall had called Braun to the front once again to deal with yet another inconsequential matter, probably for some slave revolts.

As soon as he reached the base, he looked at the map on the diminutive planning table. His heart froze when he saw the damning maps in front of him. Over the past weeks, the "Reclamation Government" had begun a massive buildup along the German frontier, and he had been oblivious to it? He knew the Russians had unified, but invading the Reich? It was absurd! More importantly, Braun shuddered to think about what it meant for his career.

An unexpected voice made him jump: his commanding officer. "Care to explain your negligence, Generalleutenant? You've been noticeably absent from your duties." the Generaloberst demanded.

"Herr Generaloberst, I was not under the impression that these were serious rep-" Braun stammered. Suddenly, his superior slammed the table in frustration, ripping the map with a gash where the German border was.

"Do you think this is a game?!" he roared in Braun's face. "We could be attacked at any moment, all for your laying about in Moskau! I need your plan, and I need you to get your ass out there to implement it right now!"

Braun had seen what those madmen did to his fellow pilot when he crash-landed in Omsk, in 1963, during the Anarchy. Had he condemned his people to not being prepared to fight against this rabid beast? What if they got into Moskau, or Sankt Petersburg, or beyond?

Ashamed and afraid, Braun spoke up. "I apologize, sir. Fortifications will be built along with the proposed conscription for all adults and emergency defense measures. Sieg Heil!"

Despite the bluster, Braun was nervous. While the Russians were a weaker people, while they didn't have the same economy, Braun knew that Yazov's Black League had one thing: hatred. All encompassing, brutal, murderous, grasping, hatred. Any tactic, any sacrifice, any idea, no matter how depraved or brutal, would be thrown at the noble German people to annihilate them.

title: Under Lock And Key
desc:
Marin closed his diary, sighing and looking out the window at the street below. As he did so, his thoughts ached at him. Thoughts of his dear lover, Sasha. He hadn’t been able to see her for a while, and the heartache he felt grew more prominent within his mind each and every day it continued.

He sat up straight, a plan forming in his mind. His eyes shot over to the clock, revealing that the 10 PM curfew would be in effect minutes from now. Marin began to pace around the room, running his hands through his hair as he considered his options. He could wait yet another night, which would probably be yet another sleepless one. So he decided to run the gauntlet, and finally see his dear lover and soulmate for the first time in months.

As he set his feet out on the pathway, he found the brightness of the moon above him both a blessing and a curse, as the first League patrols proceeded to begin the sweeping of the streets. Quietly moving behind whatever could pass for cover, he expertly maneuvered around easily a dozen patrols. Soon, he was only a block away from his dear Sasha. Smiling, he reveled in his progress so far. And it was then that he tripped, letting out a blood curdling scream into the darkness.

He immediately stood up, knowing exactly what was coming for him. Marin could only put faith into his speed, as the flashlights of patrols bounced off of the walls in front of him, soon accompanied by the terrifying sounds of gunshots. But, he did have a lead on the soldiers, and he turned the final corner, almost at the finish line. Sasha's apartment couldn’t have been more than a hundred feet away.

But...something started to burn in his back...he grew weak, losing all strength in his legs as he fell into a pool of blood. Through ever darkening vision, he saw the horrified face of his lover, who had opened her window to see where the noises were coming from. As the two locked eyes, Marin summoned one last bit of strength. He died with a smile on his lips, as his final thoughts only contained love and happiness.

options.name: The last candles of hope in Russia are being snuffed out.

title: Fortresses Among The Tundra
desc:
Andrei joined the Black League to avenge the family he’d lost in the Second Trial. To reclaim Moscow. To destroy the Teuton, once and for all. Digging a trench on the steppes of European Russia was a far cry from that. He was in an endless cycle: he'd wake up, eat breakfast, dig, eat lunch, dig more, eat dinner, dig even more, then go to sleep. It didn’t help that the ground had almost frozen solid from the weather. On top of that, it was supposed to rain the next day. Chances were, the dirt would turn to mud and undo much of their progress. It didn't matter, in Andrei's eyes. They'd been digging in the same damn spot for three weeks now and had nothing to show for it.

Once again, he plunged his shovel into the earth ahead of him once more, only to be met with a clang. He tried the same spot again a couple times, the same result producing itself each time. "Why have you stopped digging," the commissar overseeing the men demanded. "It’s the soil, sir," Andrei replied, "It’s frozen solid!"

"Then dig faster! Harder! Use your hands if you have to!"

“If you want this done faster, maybe grab your own fucking shovel and get digging,” a soldier cried. The commissar’s head snapped to the source of the demand, and he motioned with his hand for one of his guards to grab the man and bring him before him.

"What is your name, soldier?" the commissar growled. Rather than being cowed, the young soldier spit a phlegmy blob right onto the commissar's eye. The camp froze for one moment. The commissar dazedly wiped his face with a leather-bound hand.

Silently, slowly, the commissar drew his service pistol from its holster. For a split second, one could see the private attempt to struggle fruitlessly before the commissar fired a single round into his skull. His body slumped backwards into the trench. "When that bell rings, you will ignore it and keep digging," the commissar ordered.

The next morning it was raining, and as Andrei predicted, their work had been washed away.

options.name: And the private's body was never found.

title: The T.V’s will Run Black
desc:
Yustina Novikova was doing her usual business in her family’s household, a small bungalow outside of Krasnoyarsk. She lived with her family of four, her two daughters Marianna and Lana, her husband Adrik and finally herself. All in all, they were lucky. Adrik was not in the front, and yet they survived, working at the local artillery factory. As she was finishing her chores for the day, Lana ran up to her. Lana was a very artistic child and she often showed her art to her mother. This day she had made a rather terrifying piece.

The drawing looked like a demon with a German helmet languishing in pain while it burned upon a stake of fire. Around the stake were multiple people cheering as the Teuton burned. The drawing was comically unrealistic and simple, yet disturbing to look at. Yustina carefully handed the drawing back to Lana.

"See? It’s a German burning, like teacher said they should! I saw it on T.V! I hate the evil Teutons!" Lana shouted in childish rage. Yustina couldn't muster much of a response to her outbursts — they terrified her. "Do you also hate them, mommy?"

"Well, Lana... hate is a scary thing. Very scary." she offered.

Lana frowned. "But Mommy, school says that hating the enemy is good. And the 'clab-rat-ors' sold us out!"

"I just think you shouldn't draw these things, honey." Yustina sighed.

Lana frowned and crumpled the drawing in her round little hands. "Well, I'll tell the teacher you won't let me!"

Yustina grabbed Lana by the shoulder before she could scamper off. "You will do no such thing! You'll do as I say! Throw that drawing away, and don't you dare tell the teacher, or you won't have any dinner for a week!" her voice raised to a fever pitch in staccato tones until Lana, shuddering, sat down and cried on her little chair.
