She quickly moved to calm down her youngest child with soft, motherly tones. While what she did was necessary, Yustina sighed, not only over the drawing, but over her reaction.

options.name: Hate seeps even into the youngest ones

title: A Justified Military Reclamation
desc:
The village of Brilyakovo was awoken by the skid of truck tires and the shouting of voices as the 35th Motorized Infantry Division stormed the village. The steady footfalls of soldiers blended into those of panicked villagers, fleeing a potential German invasion.

A broad-shouldered officer contemptuously began to read out a prepared statement. “By command of the All-Russian Black League, this village is to be confiscated and turned over to the state in which it shall be used in our national defense. Any resistance to arrest will be met with gunfire at sight for treason."

Fearing the terror of the League, one by one, the villagers gave themselves up to the occupiers. Black-cloaked soldiers stomped to their houses, rounded the pedestrians up, and sent them to the village square. Any who resisted were beaten, or if they were unlucky, shot. Following this, they were corralled off to a few trucks, who'd send them away from everything they held dear. Only a scant 15 mix of rebellious youth and aging elders protested. However, instead of pushing and shoving, the officer simply began reading from a list of crimes they'd apparently committed against Russia.

Then, the officer raised his gloved hand, snapped his fingers, and the group was no more. In ten minutes, they were thrown into a snowy ditch. In just four hours, nothing and nobody remained. The good people of Russia would later learn that they were "attacked by Nazi Sympathizers" during the construction of state infrastructure. Despite the errant rumbling, nobody seemed to care, and certainly nobody did anything about it.

The construction was underway, and progress was steady. The village was going to become a military base for the preparations for the Great Trial. The forward military base would serve as a vanguard in the assault towards the plunderers in "Moskowien". This station, merely one of many, will be crucial in our fight against the Teutonic Menace.

options.name: An inevitable act for a noble cause.

title: This Is My Shovel
desc:
Life in the city of Dimitrovgrad was one of constant struggle for the people living there. Ever since 1941, it seemed that the residents of the average city could never truly catch a break. But recently, it seemed like they could, after Yazov had the previous owners of the city "decommissioned", life in Dimitrovgrad continued on without any real issues from the government, other than the odd military recruitment drives and so-on.

It was nice, but it couldn't last forever.

Early morning, on another seemingly average day, about five dozen soldiers poured into the city. They began going door to door and ordering the two most fit members of the family outside, once they had 52 people total. All of them odered into trucks, where they were told they were needed by the army and woulld fulfill their patriotic duty on this day.

Any questions asked were waved off and were replied with "When we arrive there, our commander will explain.". When they did arrive, all of them were ordered to dismount and line-up in age order. An officier in full League gard approached, and began to speak with a voice that exuded authority and confidence. "That way" he pointed "Is the Germans. High command has issued an express order that we should be prepared in-case any fights were to break out between us and them. So, you are going to dig two kilometers of trenches. By digging these trenches you are saving the lives of servicemen of the Russian Army. Get to work!"

And so they did Digging trenches was hard work that not all of them were used to, but with the amount of people there, it took them only about 3 hours to get the job completed to the officer's approval. Without so much as a word of praise they were then right after directed to leave the area immediately. They got back into the trucks and were driven back to the city. There were no words shared on the truck ride back, but it was obvious what everyone sitting there was thinking.

options.name: The dawn of the Great Trial was rapidly approaching.

title: Little Eyes, Little Ears
desc:
Arseniy tread with haste throughout the hallway of the bureau, folders in hand, a line to the United States straight behind the cold metal doors in front of him. He swung them open with great elan, slamming them into the utilitarian, off-white spackle. He set the folders down on the counter and booted up the computers. He jogged through the room, fiddling with knobs, setting the radios to the right frequency to call for help. The fax machine was already on, as he hoped. Everything was going swimmingly, and if it continued to do so, no one would ever know that Arseniy Nikolaev set foot in this building.

He’d had enough of it. Every day his son, Nikita, would come back from school, ranting about whatever new insanity the League invented that week, drilling him to become the perfect meat shield for the coming German onslaught. Every day his wife came back home more depressed, the tears of a woman separated from her family by the cadre system staining his white dress shirt. All of it, he’d had fucking enough. What the Americans knew was only a HINT of the true depravity of the League; soon enough, they’d get their impetus to act, god willing.

Arseniy was lost in thought until he realized something. The computers weren’t connecting to a network. The radios returned nothing but static. And the fax machine was on, but it wasn’t even working. His heart sank. The doors thumped as three men ran into the room, pistols in hand. At their front was Igor, the only officer of the League he ever managed to get along with, and the only friend he had ever made in the brutal rearrangement of the cadre system.

Igor thumbed the trigger on his pistol. “Arseniy. It is disappointing to find you here, truly.”

“H-How?”

“You raised a good kid.” Igor cocked the hammer of his gun and raised it up to Arseniy’s head.

options.name: “He’ll make a fine officer, one day.”

title: True League Comrades
desc:
In all of Ivan's life, he’d never once dared to betray the League. They were his protectors, and the ones who would strike down all who opposed his people’s enemies. And although he was only sixteen years of age, he believed himself to perhaps be the Leagues most faithful servant, taking every beating and scolding as a gift rather than a simple exercise of discipline.

Which is why he didn’t complain about being assigned to a League production facility. Upon arrival, he was in awe of the scale of these facilities, and just how intricately they were laid out. He had been assigned to a Cadre upon arrival, and was given instruction on how to operate the equipment on the production line by a fellow member of that Cadre. Within the hour, Ivan was working to produce the mechanisms of war that would assist in his nation's struggle.

He was perhaps the most zealous one there, being the first of a new type of Russian who had spent a majority of their time growing up knowing only the League and its constant flow of propaganda.

Ivan’s zealotry was exactly what the League needed, but he was a curse for the man sitting next to him, Valentin. He had never wanted to be here, and was forcefully assigned here years ago. He knew what happened to those who spoke out against the conditions, but had begun to reach his limit as the years went on. And when that day came, just a few hours after this new arrival had been assigned to work next to him, a man in an all black uniform came to inform them all of the new increase of production quotas, and the reduction in hours for break time.

He couldn’t restrain himself any longer, and let out a small whisper of defiance. “I hate this place and the godforsaken fools that lead it.”

Ivan heard every word. He swung his head over to look at the fool who dared speak against the League, but didn’t say a word. Later that day, he would report it to an official. And when he went to sleep, his bunkmate Valentin was there.

options.name: When he awoke, he was gone.

title: Great Russian Murals
desc:
Pavel wiped the sweat from his forehead, admiring the finished poster design. Like all his other works as of late, it had been commissioned. Well, 'commissioned' was a deeply charitable way of saying 'he had been told by a large, threatening man in a uniform to make it on pain of death whilst on minimal wages', but he was holding onto as much positivity as he could muster, given the circumstances.

He looked down upon what he had drawn, and felt alongside the token pride he took in his work, the familiar taste of bitterness. He was a cartoonist by trade. An illustrator. Before the Black League marched into his smaller city in West Russia, he had drawn cartoons of small animal people for children, living life and teaching them how to be kind to one another. His style had certainly developed over the years, that was for sure. Certainly not of his own volition, however.

Where he had once drawn soft, rounded shapes to appeal to the younger eye, he now drew sharp, angular lines. Lessons on life and getting along with one another were of no use to the Black League, nor was softness — only messages of triumph over the Teuton and the superiority of the Russian spirit would do. This was embodied in his piece — a chiseled man in a Black League uniform snapping the neck of Adolf Hitler.

The old artist sighed, looking at the time. 3:56AM. He still had 5 prompts to produce art for. Part of him wanted to doodle absent-midedly, but his paper usage was cataloged and he would be penalized financially for any 'wasted' paper. He checked the list once again. His next prompt, 'Russian Eagle disembowelling a German Eagle" would be fun to draw. Hopefully.

options.name: No room for creativity in the Great Trial.

title: A Safe Frontline
desc:
Pavel wiped the sweat from his brow, as his shovel dug into the dirt once more. He’d lost track of how long he’d been training, digging, building, and preparing for when his country would at last strike the Aryan, and drown him in his own blood. His brigade's training regimens had grown even more demanding than usual, but nobody complained. Every man knew what it was for, and some even welcomed the new torment brought upon them.

After all, every drop of blood, every broken bone, every moment of pain, was fuel. Fuel for the brave sons and daughters of the League who would exact vengeance on those who had defiled her, who had broken her and believed her incapable of returning to the world. Yet here they stood, ready to tear those scum limb from limb as the west burned in the fires of vengeance.

Pavel looked up from his part of the defensive works, and for the first time saw in their entirety the fruits of his and his comrades' work. Trenches and bunkers for miles, with a multitude of differently designed defensive works dug into the earth around them. Sadly his time for admiration quickly ended with the commanding officer's orders to get into formation. Pavel and his fellow soldiers assembled within seconds, forming an intricate pattern with each one standing at attention and ready for orders.

“Soldiers, I have received new orders pertaining to the extension of drilling procedures within the League. You shall now have only three separate five minute break periods per day, and you are required to complete a daily 12 mile run in place of the pre-existing 10 mile run. However, with the completion of all defensive works projects in this sector, you’re no longer to assist in their construction. Finally, the minimum accuracy in shooting range tests has been increased to 90%. Dismissed.”

Pavel and his 2 other friends found each other during the break period, and began to talk about things to come. Not about the new, unbelievably difficult demands laid upon their shoulders, but about a topic they had been betting upon for a while.

They each argued who would be the first to enter Moscow.

options.name: The warriors of a new age...

title: Burn Evidence, Burn Witnesses
desc:
Rule 15. Should a suspected person be found disseminating misinformation that undermines progress of the Great Trial, they are to be taken from their living area and put into interrogation until they reveal exactly which Teuton agency they are working for and who they have lied to. Upon revealing this, said person is to be executed.

Rule 16. Should a member of the police or any other security agency come into contact with any misinformative or deceptive Teuton propaganda, it is to be taken to the nearest town pyre and thrown in with any other Germanic materials. Only the cleansing fires can bring any merit out of their sordid materials.

Rule 17. Should a civilian act out against any member of the Black League or other official personnel, they are to be subdued by any means necessary. Punishment for doing so can range from two decades of service in a labor camp, rescindment of nuclear protections, a reduction of rations to any known familial relations, or point blank execution.

title: The Weaponization of Social Progress
desc:
It was odd, having Yuri out of the house so often. Nadya wandered through their shared apartment, as she often did nowadays, wafting aimlessly from room to room. The couple had only met recently, a few years ago at a book club in Tomsk. Yuri had always been a well-read man.

Part of her wanted to be distraught that her partner had been forced into working 14-hour shifts at the local munitions factory, seven days a week, and she was undoubtedly angry at not seeing him as much. But whilst he was gone, she had found herself digging into the secret stash of books that Yuri kept, hidden away where the Black League couldn't burn it for not being patriotic enough.

He was always too scared to share his collection with her, before. But because he was now too busy to even come close to stopping her, Nadya could do it, and when she did, she felt free. And she enjoyed that feeling more than anything.

Of course, she knew that Yazov had not done this out of some great feminist desire to liberate women, or something. Russia was not the place for that. But he had done something, inadvertently. As she curled up with Yuri's copy of War and Peace, Nadya mused about what else to do later on. It wasn't as if she'd be pressed for time, after all.

title: An Ear In Every Room
desc:
Nikolai Volkov was not a man to take things lightly. Suspicion was as much a part of his personality as his affinity for black tea or his love for classic Russian novels. Living in an aging apartment complex, he had a habit of paying a little too much attention to his surroundings.

This particular night was no exception. As the small town settled into its nocturnal routine, an unusual hush fell over his apartment. However, what caught his attention was the soft murmur of his neighbors' conversation seeping through the paper-thin wall separating their lives.

His heart pounded slightly harder in his chest, the tranquility of his demeanor replaced with an edge of anxiety. The conversation felt different, the cadence, the intensity. Even the silence between their words seemed to carry a certain gravity. Something was not right.

The words were veiled by the sturdiness of the wall, the specific sentences hard to decipher. Yet, certain phrases seemed to penetrate this barrier, filling his apartment, and his mind, with an unease. "It's coming sooner than we thought," he heard a man say. "We need to prepare. It could change everything," a woman responded.

A shiver ran down Nikolai's spine, his eyes narrowing with intrigue and suspicion. Was it a coded message? Could his seemingly ordinary neighbors be involved in some clandestine operation? As the minutes rolled into hours, he found himself increasingly drawn to this puzzle and soon enough found the answer in his troubled mind.

He rushed to pick up his old telephone and dial 'Line One.' A heavily distorted voice echoed through the receiver, “You have reached the Complaints Secretariat, do you have a concern to report?”

Drawing in a deep breath, Nikolai found the words he needed, the declaration that felt both chilling and necessary, "I do. I think my neighbors are spies.”

options.name: “It’s a boy, Anatoly... it’s a boy...”

title: Produce Only What You Need
desc:
A loud knock was on the door followed by an order to open the door immediately. A worker rushed to the door and opened it. It was a Black League officer. The officer demanded to speak to the owner. He said that this factory had been creating too many luxury products and should instead focus on producing only what the community and army needs. The workers called the owner out. The owner was annoyed, but came quickly.

“What is i-”

His heart stopped whenever he saw the officer.

“Your factory has been deemed to not be complying with the government's regulations. You have been creating too many luxury goods.”

The owner started biting his nails, he knew that it was illegal to produce luxury goods, however it was very lucrative and had generated an immense amount of wealth for him.

“Are you insane? You fools are destroying Russia! How are we supposed to earn a living here if business can’t flourish without the government sticking their nose where they shouldn’t!”

“I will not repeat myself, cease production or else you will be terminated.”

The owner thought for a moment. Would he really be willing to sacrifice all of this wealth just for some doomed war? Why did they have to come into power? Russia would’ve been prosperous under any other government but we had to get stuck with these fools.

“Mere bluffing will not stop me. I am one of the biggest industrialists in all of Russia, do you really think you can terminate me without any consequences?”

The officer sighed, and calmly reached for his pistol.

title: Acceptance is Defeat
desc:
Rows of workers, hoping to find some respite from the grueling labor that was their lives from dawn to dusk, were instead sitting before a projector, soldiers in black uniforms guarding the exits. A few of the workers squirmed in their chairs, the uncomfortable seating compounding the aching in their muscles. At the front of them all stood an officer, gesturing to the wall on which the projection was playing.

"Here you see the bodies of the dead. The German beasts have mutilated their corpses for the crime of rebellion. These are your fellow Russians, those who seek to be redeemed in the struggle against our eternal foe. This is what they are doing at this very moment, and what they hope to do to all of us should they succeed in their plans."

The film showed a mass grave that had been dug by some of the other slaves working in the Reichskommissariat Moskowien. Men, women, and children were lying in a mountain of bodies, with bullet holes and gashes where bayonets had pierced their skin. The film then shifted as a group of soldiers harassed a woman who had attempted to kill one of the officers. They tore at her clothing, enough for the men to begin raping her. Some of the workers looked away on instinct, not wanting to continue watching. Only the mere movement of the men in black out of the corner of their eyes snapped their attention back towards the projection.

After the men had finished with her, one of them took out a knife and began stabbing her. A game of sorts had started as the soldiers began cutting at her as if to carve mementos from her body. She was only screaming for a few short moments before she lay dead. By the end, she was missing both her ears, a hand, and a breast, and her stomach had been cut open. The film ended here.

"See the hatred that the Germans feel for us, and know that we will show them retribution. They will feel our wrath–our vengeance–and justice will be served to every last one of them."[Change Later]

options.name: Shock and horror give way to rage.

title: Goodbyes at Fifteen
desc:
The bugle’s call clawed at the morning fog, yanking Ivan from his thin mattress. Cold and barefoot, the fifteen-year-old recruit snapped to attention like he had done every day for the past five months. Thirty-two other recruits of similar age fell into formation next to their beds, an unbroken line of adolescent determination stretching down the length of the barracks.

Exactly twenty-three seconds after the horn sounded, their drill officer stormed into the room. His eyes held a glint that spoke of a perpetual bad mood and a determination to instil order and discipline in his charges.

"Kozlov! Fix that blasted posture now!" His words sliced through the morning chill. "Are you planning on marching into Germany looking like a hunchback?"

Kozlov stumbled over his response, the young cadet wilting under scrutiny. "Y-yes sir! It won’t happen again."

"Damn right it won't," growled the officer. His gaze swept over them all, eyes as piercing and cold as the winds outside. "We are the chosen, the ones to reclaim our homeland's glory. We are the instruments of the Great Trial, and we will not fail!" His gaze found Ivan's, a silent understanding passing between them. "Ivanov," he said, a new edge of severity cutting through his voice, "You were the first to arrive at the training field yesterday, were you not?"

"Yes sir, I was." Ivan's voice held steady under the scrutiny.

The officer grunted, a sound trapped between approval and scorn. "Good. Make sure you're the first one today as well, or it's extra drills for you."

As the officer moved on, Ivan set his gaze straight ahead, a grim smile tugging at his lips. His day had just begun. The whispered dreams of home from the night before lingered, but there was no time for dreams here, only duty.

options.name: The Motherland has no need for sentimentalism.

title: Baubles and Trinkets
desc:
The disgusting symbols of Nazis are what they were. Baubles, flags, and other assorted items were strewn along the side of the road. The Black League had crushed these men like the vermin they were. They were Nazi worshipers, whether they believed themselves distinct or not. Anyone who called himself an Aryan wasn't worth a second thought as you crushed their head beneath your boot, painting the snow with their brain. Ivan smirked as he looked over the baubles, swinging his rifle over his shoulder. "Come over, boys. Let's take a look!" He shouted to his comrades.

There were pins which were meant to be attached to lapels, as well as drawings of vikings swinging their swords at monsters and creatures. These degenerates probably truly believed that this shit was real. "Take a look at this one," Ivan said as he picked up one of the drawings and showed it to one of his fellow soldiers. "You think whoever owned this one thought he would swing his Aryan sword at us and cast us into the pits of hell?"

"Who knows what the hell they thought. They're dead, that's what's important." The soldier replied, kicking some dirt and snow onto the collection. "This should all be burned before someone reads it and their mind is poisoned by these degenerates." In reply, the other soldiers laughed, a rolling laughter that left some of them on their hands and knees against the dirt road.

"You," Ivan replied through laughs, "put far too much power into these degenerates' words. Who in their right minds would follow fanatics like these?" He patted the soldier on his back, before rounding up his men and continuing down the road.

They were close to the next village and as they approached, they could see a fire burning in the center of the village. On closer examination, there was a viking-like statue carved out of wood in the center of the village. It wasn't very well made; clearly created by peasantry. But around the statue, wood was stacked up and set aflame. And around the flaming wood were the residents of this village, all laying in red snow, dead. Their throats were cut, and each of them held a knife. Nothing was left alive in the village except the ravens cawing on the rooftops.

options.name: Even a fanatic's words hold sway.

title: The Prototype
desc:
Chains rattling. Fires burning. Hunger, thirst, sadness, death. This is the scene that Dmitry Yazov bore witness to upon a tour of the camps set up in the wake of the defeat of the “Aryan” Brotherhood. After stepping out of his car, Yazov locked eyes with a young man, emaciated and near-death, faintly looking onto him with a look of disgust and hatred. Looking at him for a moment, Yazov entered the small barbed-wire enclosure that houses these degenerate souls. Looking over upon these starving, dirty, and broken men, Yazov feels a mixture of contempt and regret. These animals, who enslaved innocent Russians, who slaughtered without thought, and who were fully convinced that this would bring them salvation, were now brought down to their knees, and silently begging for any kind of mercy to come to them. These thoughts only entered Yazov’s head for a moment, however, as soon he would be greeted by the Administrative team running the camp.

“I trust you had a safe Journey in, sir?” said one of the younger Administrators, with a tinge of intimidation in his voice.

“Can I trust that these traitors to the Russian people are being taken care of?” Said Yazov, aggressively.

“This filth? They are giving us an hour of work for every single Russian child who never saw their father again!” said one of the more senior administration members “They will all redeem themselves through blood, sir. In due time.”

Yazov glanced around the room and then back at the man speaking to him. “Very well. These animals, wishing to purge all who do not bear loyalty to their hooked cross. But these men are not the issues, my friends. They are simply side-effects of a much larger phenomenon, and soon, very soon, all of those who wish ill upon the Russian state will find them paying a very large debt back to the motherland!

options.name: These men have hell to pay.

title: The Last Will
desc:
The room rattled ferociously as the lights continued to flicker, growing dimmer with each passing moment. Despite the layers of concrete and steel, the horrors that lay on the surface could never truly be masked. Georgy Zhukov, Marshal of the ever shrinking Soviet Union, grasped his aging microphone, both to steady its rusty frame and his frail body.

He looked up. Where once secretaries, staff, comrades had stood, now there was only silence. It seemed he alone would tend to the worker's flame in its darkest hour. He looked down. His hastily prepared speech was more akin to the stumbling of a dying spider than the words of a great statesman, but it would serve him nonetheless. As the room at last grew still, the Marshal began his final, but perhaps his most important, oration...

"Soldiers and citizens, friends and foes, masters and serfs, I come to you bearing the hopes and fears of myself and my nation alike. Despite the heights we have risen to, despite the enemies we have destroyed, despite the continuing temerity of our people, our banner will not fly forever. The Dark forces of the Black League have overwhelmed our nascent union and again killed the flower of our country's youth. This will be my final address.

But peoples' of the world! Do not despair! Our cause may be over, but there is hope for you still. The insidious Yazov wishes to open his own version of Pandora's box. Chemical, biological, nuclear, they will destroy everyone they deem their enemy, no matter their creed or character. They will take the world with them, too.

If they are allowed to conquer and exploit unabated, humanity as a concept will end. I beg of everyone listening, suspend your petty divisions, and unite against this tidal wave of horrors. I beg of everyone, there can be no despondence or delay, I beg-"

"Get on the ground. Now!"

" As the once empty room filled with masked soldiers, Grigory Zhukov, the Black League's newest prisoner, collapsed to the floor. But pain did not forsake him, for despite his age, his flaws, and his failures, he had done today what he had set out to do.

He simply hoped that the world had heard.

title: The Siege of Arkangelsk
desc:
The tension in the command bunker was oppressive. All of the senior generals of the Red Army stood around a large table with a map depicting the city of Arkangelsk. Small black figurines were placed on the map in a semicircle ring from coast to coast, leaving no doubt that the city was surrounded. Tukhachevsky stared at those black figurines, his scowl deepening with each passing moment as he was forced to acknowledge just how bad things had become.

"Perhaps, Grand Marshal, it might be time to consider escape..." One of the younger generals finally spoke up. Tukhachevsky looked over to him, but said nothing. He took this to mean that he may continue, and so he explained, "There is still the coastline, which we have control over. We could organize a retreat across the White Sea and into Finland, and from there into Sweden."

"The Finns would love to get their hands on some reds," Another general said. "We'll have to be careful when we move through their territory. Does anyone here know Finnish?"

"No." Tukhachevsky interrupted this talk of retreat. His eyes were still locked on the young general's face. The man's hair was still full of color, and his face only showed the beginning wrinkles of age and decay. This supposed soldier thought that his youth gave him the privilege of living longer. He seemed to forget... no, all of them had forgotten what it means to be fighting men. They were soldiers, and they would not abandon their posts. Not under his command.

"You are all cowards." Tukhachevsky spoke calmly, his anger simmering just beneath the surface. "You propose to run like frightened children across the frozen wastes and leave the Russian people to toil under that madman's control? Are you not Communists? You are the Red fucking Army! We will fight them in every alleyway and across every street corner until this city is laid to rubble and then we shall fight them over the scraps that remain. And we will win. I don't want to hear any more talk of surrender. If Yazov wants to take Arkangelsk, he'll have to kill every last one of us

options.name: The Red Napoleon gives his last speech.

title: Memorandum No. 4, 568
desc:
[Change Later]"From the desk of Glavkoverkh Dmitri Timofeyevich Yazov, leader of our nation and follower of our founder Dmitry Karbyshev:

Today, I write with a sense of satisfaction. Our operation to bring the impotent and disunited opponents of our rightful mission was quick, clean, and showed neither hesitancy nor mercy. Every single man who has marched west in these recent months has done their job dutifully, and they have done it well. I congratulate every one of you.

However, I believe that this recent victory may serve as a good point of reflection as to the righteousness of both our goals and the way in which we achieve them. Suppose that, every time us men of battle wished to conduct a maneuver, complete a task, instruct an individual, everyone, no matter their rank or their relevance, had to be consulted. Imagine, if you will, that every single decision made had to be checked, authorized, reauthorized, and passed through a myriad of near infinite bureaucracy. How then, would our operation have gone. Would it have been quick, clean, and merciless?

Every man who has so much as picked up a rifle thus knows the folly that is democracy. Every man who has so much as worked in a team knows that cohesion, competence, and decisiveness is reliant on resolute action, ascribed from men who have earned elevated rank, and followed without question by those beneath them. Every man today now knows why our Black League operates the way it does.

But do not grow feeble and meek. The treacherous Teutons know of this too, for they have abandoned the feebleness of democracy just as we have done the same. When we march west once more, they will not be as forgiving.

Whether all of you rise to the challenge remains to be seen.

title: Simple Arithmetic
desc:
Name: Igor Shafarevich

Occupation: President of the Russian Republic.

Previous Occupations: Mathematics Professor, Writer, Radio Talk Show Host, Political Dissident.

Status: HVT-1099-A surrendered peacefully with the occupation of Syktyvkar and Vyatka. Signed terms of conditional surrender. Currently in custody and awaiting trial-

"A mathematician?" Yazov crumpled the paper and tossed it into the trash. "What an absurdity."

He stood and looked out of the snow-flecked window that adjoined his office. What a  joke. The people of Russia elected a mathematician and allowed him to create a state calling itself a 'republic'. A 'democracy'. A system of snakes. A system of inefficiency, mistreatment, and deception. A weak, degenerate system.

Yazov looked into the training ground outside his office. There, newly commissioned officers were undergoing physical and mental conditioning — the same training their subordinates had already survived. The Black League would not permit the unworthy to lead the strong. No. The comrades of the League would lift their subordinates by their iron wills, and the enlisted would lift  their leaders by their obedience.

Not so, in a democracy. Yazov's men had already lifted the curtain. Anti-semitism, bribery, and corruption were rife in Shafarevich's fief. More commonly, representatives simply ignored what they'd campaigned on to suck at the teat of graft. An unacceptable division in a time of civilizational struggle. No, the Russians who suffered Shafarevich's inferior vision were not free. Once again, the Black League marched as liberators. Once again, they brought freedom.

"Freedom," Yazov whispered. "Freedom is ... " He struggled to find the words. Not from a piece of paper, he knew, not from the childish whims of a parliament. Not from the civilized rituals of legislation. "Freedom is strength. Strength is freedom."

And thus, he realized, the Black League is freedom.

options.name: No mathematician can calculate their fall.

title: Death Call Of the Steppes
desc:
Glavkoverkh Yazov entered the vacant Passionarity congress hall. It reeked of gin and dried urine. A caustic taste tingled on the tip of his tongue. "You found the hall in this manner, Private?"

Private Artemyev nodded. "Sir, yes sir. We eliminated the Eurasian milita sent to defend the hall three clicks from the building." The Private smiled, excitement creeping into his voice. "Ambushed them, sir. They weren't ready for us."

"You have nothing to be proud of, Private." Yazov ran a finger over a wooden banister. Dust. "Look around you. Look at these cave paintings. Look at the standard our enemies held themselves to. This room speaks to me of ineptitude, and cultural insignificance."

The Private began to sweat. "I apologize, sir."

"We do not permit ourselves self-aggrandizement, soldier." Yazov shook his head. "Our enemies debased themselves, physically and ideologically. Their thoughts were born of an artificial rationale, not rooted in tradition or actual culture but instead a false preconception of history. Lev Gumilyev -" a vein bulged on Yazov's forehead " — sought to erase Russia's cultural reality, and reorganize our people into a mindless horde. The same horde, mind you, that raped and pillaged our nation centuries ago. They were nothing more than barbarians. And this was nothing more than pest control."

Private Artemyev stood as still as stone. The wooden floor creaked beneath their feet.

Yazov raised his head to the rafters. "I would not be proud of shooting rats, Private. I advise you to keep your attention on duty." He raised an eyebrow. "Now, please light this garbage on fire."[Change Later]

options.name: Passion alone could not save them.

title: Last Stand of Madness
desc:
An RPG soared through the sky and exploded in a fireball against Taboritsky's grand palace. The fine marble and gold inlays were ruined from three days of heavy gunfire. The Black League fired from all directions, unleashing a hailstorm of brass and the mighty thunder of cannons. The defenders knelt in trenches, their cover whittling away, praying that God would intervene and save the Holy Regent.

The League's soldiers saw an opening, and squads flooded the palace grounds. Fervent guards stood their ground, some felled by a single bullet, others taking a few more. Afterwards, a handful of attackers swore they saw a man with ragged hair and bloodshot eyes stand up even after a round pierced his lung.

The agonizing slog of claiming the compound section by section took the rest of the afternoon. Every corridor, every room, every hall was trapped, every corner held an ambush. When Taboritsky's men ran out of ammunition, they turned to knives and blood streaked fists.

By the end of the day, the League claimed five hundred and eighty six scalps. The few who were captured refused to repent their allegiance. They showed no regret, and died believing in their own righteousness. But of the many, many corpses, none belonged to Taboritsky. The League's men double-checked, triple-checked, and, with the guiding hand of the Interrogation Cadres, quadruple checked. Their conclusion remained the same: Regent Taboritsky had escaped.

The League's leadership ground its teeth and wailed its anger. Orders were given, subordinates punished. But they could not overawe the joy in the hearts of soldiers and civilians alike as the disgraceful flag of the Holy Russian Empire lowered from its pole. Taboritsky's twisted vision for Russia was grounded into dust, here, forever.

title: Memorandum No. 45,862
desc:
From the desk of Glacoverk Dimitry Timofeyevich Yazov, leader of our nation and follower of our founder Karbyshev:

I congratulate all of you Russians who have participated in this great pacification operation of the tyrannical dictator Ivan Serov. As many of you know, and as much as that mentally ill troglodyte has tried to establish, Ordosocialism is dead.

His ideals of Fascist Communism is fundamentally a broken system. Many years ago, when the Black League broke from the yolk of the West Siberian Socialist Republic, Karbyshev and now I made a promise to never submit to the opiates of Communism and Bukharanist thought. That the ideals of Marx, Lenin, and all other socialist revolutionaries have done nothing to truly help people. They have led the Russian people astray.

Was it not that Lenin was sent on a train from Switzerland to the old Monarchy due to the German menace? And was it not that Marx and Engels were Germans? Clearly these two snakes have had the ability to run rampant throughout all of Russia and Ordosocialism is the final binding of Communism with their Germanic origin. I, personally, am happy that we have aborted this way of thought before it festered within our great nation long enough.

The only saving grace that this unredeemable man has accomplished within his borders of Western Russia was his industrial programs. He has turned the nation into a factory, albeit one of fear and hate. We shall begin using these facilities to create better weapons of war in order to fully blot out the German cloud.

Thank you.

title: Recursive Failures
desc:
Yazov looked at the plethora of military reports on his desk, this was it. Victory in Western Russia had been achieved, the resilient and loyal soldiers of the Black League had marched across the Urals and swiftly crushed any resistance. He put down the pile of papers, before slumping over in his chair.

The Soviet Union was gone; left shattered by the Germanic marauders in the First Trial. The deceitful, incompetent ways of Bukharin cascading Russa into chaos. Yazov thought of his time fighting on the Eastern Front, forced to retreat beyond the A-A line, humiliated by the Union's failures. Oh, the young Soviet Union was his homeland, one he was supposed to defend and feel a sense of patriotism for, but seeing Bukharin's failures first hand, it shed a light on its shortcomings. In what was the tragedy of what was the fall of the U.S.S.R, something could be salvaged: information. If the Black League ever needed to survive, it needed the knowledge of how to avoid the faults of the Union.

But Yazov knew that knowledge was a fickle thing, some people were stubborn enough to deliberately copy the mistakes of the past, and Bukharina was no exception. She was like a caricature of her father, showing the worst parts of him. All this talk of "Marxist dialectics", "the proletariat", but how does this serve the Russian people beyond pseudo-intellectual discussion? The Soviet Union was gone, and Bukharina's death cemented it.

options.name: The hydra pervading Russia has been slayed.

title: MEMORANDUM 93: Communist Ideology
desc:
From the desk of Glavkoverkh Dmitry Timofeyevich Yazov, leader of our nation and follower of our founder Dmitry Karbyshev:

I write having just been informed of the unconditional surrender of the treacherous communist government of Mikhail Suslov. I would like to take this opportunity to reflect on communism and its effects on our nation.

I was once a communist. Communism and its proponents have long held admirable goals for Russia. It saved us from complete destruction following the civil war, and brought some measure of economic strength to our nation. I grew up in Bukharin’s Russia, and I joined Bukharin’s Red Army in 1941 to fight the Teutonic menace. Later, I joined the Revolutionary Front and took up arms once again in the West Russian War. Throughout this time, I believed in communism, and its vision of a truly strong and prosperous Russia.

However, I need not remind anyone that both Red Armies I fought in ultimately lost, undermined by petty squabbling and weak idealism of their political leadership. This is where the lofty ideals of Lenin and Bukharin fall apart. They cannot survive the siege that we, the Russian nation, find ourselves under. The Germanic horde cannot be fought with equality, it cannot be fought with dialectics, it cannot even be fought with prosperity. No, the Teutons can only be fought with steel. Violence alone is our defense against the arsenal the Teutons bring against them, of which communism is in fact a component. Need I remind you where Marx, the inventor of this Germanic corruption of the Russian nation, comes from? Need I remind you that Lenin himself was sent here by the Teutons to undermine us in the Great War?

Communism is not a defense for the Russian nation, nay, it is yet another sword pointed by the Teutons at our heart.

title: Report BP-DPL-WQ8
desc:
Identifier: BP-DPL-WQ8

Composer: BLP-NV-3

Classification: 2A+

Concerning: Salvage of People's Commissariat of Science

Background: Following capitulation of Soviet Federation, Scientific Cadre 112685 ordered to amass, investigate, and identify useful research and 'blue sky' technologies developed by the People's Commissariat of Science. Interrogation Cadre 356707 ordered to interrogate surviving Federation personnel to accomplish this objective.

Findings: Ninety-five percent of technologies recorded in People's Commissariat archives classified by 112685 as Class Zero (Not Recommended for Further Inquiry). Further three percent classified as Class One (Potential Civilian Applications) and two percent classified as Class Two (Potential Military Applications). Personnel note that scientific research in the Federation was driven by political concerns and as a method of personal aggrandisement rather than potential use cases. Additionally, personnel note possible logistics concerns with technologies in Class Two category, as many will require heavy industrial investment to be produced at a significant scale.

One item noted as Class Three (Immediate Military Applications). Project CHEREPAKHA is a long distance, supersonic bomber. Existing data and blueprints indicate measurable superiority over current Black League air assets in both speed, resilience, and air power. Further information in Appendix A-74-SSI (attached).

One item noted as Class Four (Immediate and Significant Military Applications). Project CHERENKOV is a re-engineered medium tank design involving a number of design superiorities including mobility over rough terrain, decreased reload time, and armor plating designed to minimize the effects of radiation exposure to crew. Recommend immediate production of test models and exercises using CHERENKOV models within twelve months.

title: [Change Later]"MEMORANDUM 884: Monarchist Collaborationism"[Change Later]
desc:
[Change Later]"Comrade soldiers! We celebrate together as we rip the collaborationist parasite from our lands. The Sovereignty of Western Russia is no more. Our victory is evidence of our superiority and our righteousness. Indeed, it is the only evidence a soldier needs.

It has not escaped the soldiers who conquered the Tsar's palace that he lived in splendor while his people scraped in poverty. Monarchism is, by its nature, corrupt. By empowering men of weak bodies and corrupt minds for their bloodline, it ensures only that the nation is led by bandits, the vainglorious, and the self-obsessed. Comrade soldiers, there is only one bloodline which matters: the bloodline of Russia!

Monarchism is a yearning for the past. It denies, even despises the present, searching ever backwards for the image of power and respect. But we know that respect comes to those who earn it, and power comes not from symbols but from action.

Our Russia is a land of merit. Where the strong shall lead, and become stronger for it. Where strength of body, strength of mind, and strength of will define your duties, and your rewards. Our Russia is led by men of humble beginnings. The League is made up of diligent men of firm character, not those empowered by an accident of birth. Our Russia is a land of the present, neither indulging in fancies of the future nor denying the sorrows of the past. Our eyes are fixed on the here and now, upon duty, and upon the actions we must take to leave the precipice of annihilation.

We who have conquered the present have overturned those who obsess over the past. There is only today. There is only duty."[Change Later]

options.name: [Change Later]"And only in death does duty end."[Change Later]

title: The Traitor's Call
desc:
This had to work. There were no other options left for Bunyachenko. The League had beaten him time and again. They had driven his people from the Ural Mountains. They had driven them back to the Kama River, and they had driven them back until the only thing behind his men was the Reichskomissarat. At every engagement, the League had shown more fortitude and more cunning. They were like a steel blade cutting through his men in one clean sweep. But he would never back down or surrender. Not to them. Not to any man. He would save Russia from itself.

"Men," Bunyachenko began to speak as he paced before a few dozen soldiers, the last remnants of his army. "On the other side of this hill is the bulk of the League's army. They're tired from fighting us. They have had to travel over hundreds of miles of our land. And they have butchered everything in sight. They have laid waste to your villages, your cities, and your families. Your wives and and children may have even died at the hands of one of those monsters on the other side of that hill. And did they shed a tear for any of them? Did any of them show an ounce of mercy for the many they've killed? No.

"Let's show them what they deserve. They want to cleanse Russia of its filth? I agree. They want to purify Russia, so that it can stand strong once again as a mighty power? I couldn't agree more. And in our shared mission to free Russia of degeneracy, I say we start with the men in black over these fucking hills!"

He raised his rifle to the cheers of his men, all their eyes looking up to him with inspiration, young and old. Perhaps they could still do this. Perhaps they could pull victory from the jaws of defeat. Who knew? Yazov himself could be standing at the head of the army, and this charge might make it far enough to kill him, and leave the black snake leaderless as it eats itself from within. So many possibilities ran through Bunyachenko's mind as he turned, and charged over the hill. On the other side were hundreds of League soldiers waiting for them. And the moment enough of them had charged over the ridge, they opened fire and let their bullets spray into the bodies of Bunyachenko and his men.

title: The Negotiating Table
desc:
There must have been twenty of them. They wore black uniforms and peaked caps, each patched and repaired with scraps of the same ink colored cloth. Each of them was armed even beyond what was expected of an ROA soldier- machineguns, pistols, agglomerations of miscellaneous ammunition, knives and trunchions dangled from overful waists and bent backs. Zykov trembled whenever one grew near. He'd rather be anywhere but sitting at this dusty banquet tablel; but it was here, or a gallows.

The floor creaked as General Sakharovsky, the League's representative in these negotiations, sat down. He slid his bony hand onto the back of  Zykov's neck. "Now then, Mister President," the smirking officer said, "Let's get down to business. Your armies are decimated, and good Russians are fleeing for their lives. The League is more than happy to slaughter the surviving ROA formations in Gorky and Vologda." The General's grip tightened. "But I believe that cooler heads can prevail. I believe that, should you concede to total annexation and order the survivors of your military to stand down, the League may be inclined to commute your sentence to life imprisonment."

Zykov’s heart sank. "Gentlemen, Gentlemen," he said, desperately glancing around the room for an ally. The League's soldiers were cold, not ever glaring in anger as he pleaded. "We are civilized men here! There's no need to leave an experienced propagandist like me to rot. Surely we can work something out."

Sakhavorsky clicked his tongue. "Corporal Ivanova, could you forge the President's signature?"

One of the soldiers nodded. "Yes, sir. With enough time."

The General smiled. "Well, it seems we don't need you after all, President Aleksandrovich. It has been a pleasure."

Before Zykov could respond, two men with Titanium grips grabbed him by the shoulders and pulled him from the table. He wanted to scream, he wanted to make a desperate plea, to beg for his life. In the end, all that escaped his mouth was a terrified wail.

options.name: All ROA soldiers are hereby ordered to immediately surrender. Signed, President Meletios Aleksandrovich Zykov.

title: The Great Scam Ends
desc:
The bottom of the vodka bottle never looked more beautiful. Or perhaps it was simply the fact that Oktan couldn't see it very well, with his hand swaying this way and that, and his eyes only able to make out vague shapes swimming across his vision. He still had to finish the last bit of it, though. Couldn't very well let it go to waste. So he turned the bottle over his cup, pouring out the last of it before tossing the bottle aside and letting it shatter against the hardwood of his office. He took hold of his glass, leaned back, and shot the drink down his throat, before throwing the glass over to join the bottle as shards across the floor.

He could have lived like a king. He had been using the Germans like marionettes, and they were singing to his tune just as he'd wanted. The whole of Russia could have been his domain with their help, and he could have taken whatever he fucking wanted from whoever he fucking wanted. But no. Yazov and his band of radicals had to storm across the Urals and beat back his army. What fucking use is an army if they can't defend some god damn mountains?

Oktan looked back to his desk, eyes locked on a German Luger lying on top. He reached over and took hold of it, twirling it between his fingers lazily. Perhaps he could run away with what he could carry, and live it rich in the Caribbean or South America. Somewhere tropical. But he could hear gunshots approaching from outside. He couldn't run, not anymore; Yazov's men were far too close. He wouldn't make it ten miles. No, there was nothing he could do.

He pressed the barrel against the underside of his chin, feeling the coolness of the metal spreading across his skin. He had no illusions about some supposed afterlife; once the trigger was pulled, darkness would be Oktan's eternal companion. All of the money that he's amassed won't matter. It'll all be used to fuel Yazov's war machine. The glory of leading West Russia would be swept away to the dustbin of history. Oktan would be a footnote, and nothing more. Yes, darkness was all he had left before him. He let his finger squeeze down on the trigger as he painted the wall with his head.

title: All is Lost
desc:
The city was burning. The air was choked with ash and smoke and embers, scraps of a dream deferred that drifted on the wind like fireflies. Private Koslov held his left arm over his face, hoping to ward the sting from his watering eyes. He failed. The young man, barely sixteen, stumbled over wood and rubble, his Kalashnikov clutched by the cold barrel.

In the distance, he could hear screaming. The invaders were growling, roaring their hate like animals. They had slipped past language into the primordial. Beneath their shouts, he could hear civilians — women — begging for mercy. Their speech was crushed under the hammerfall of gunshots.

Koslov's bowels ran cold. The stripling broke out in a sweat as he scrabbled through chalk and fallen beams, forcing himself forward on his hands and knees. He had to escape. He had to get away from this nightmare, retreat, live to fight another day -

"Help me." A phantom's moan drifted on the burning wind.  "Please... help me."

Koslov wiped the tears and smoke from his eyes. Everything around him was an indistinguishable ruin, the same pattern of broken concrete and toppled walls. Without thinking, the words slipped from his mouth. "W-where-" He cleared his throat, spitting black phlegm into the dust. "Where are you?"

A scraping sound came from his left, and Koslov saw him. He was a man, or the remnants of one. The soldier was middle aged, balding, with a curly grey beard and the patch of the Utopian salon's militia sewn onto the breast pocket of his uniform. And his legs had been crushed by a falling beam. An arm dangled by the man's side, useless.

Koslov knew what the soldier wanted before he even spoke. Mercy. A reprieve from the animals that hunted Tomsk's ruins. But the League was close, and growing closer by the second. He could feel their breath on his neck...

"I'm sorry." The boy turned as the soldier wailed in horror, and sprinted for the city's outskirts. For survival, and shame.

title: A Struggle Forgotten
desc:
The building had since been cleared of any sort of hostile presence, and been swept for mines and traps. Though Pavel still lingered, this previously being an administrative center, perhaps there could be something interesting here. Be it actually useful intelligence, or just simple curiosity, trivia and the like. He stubbed his cigarette out on the windowsill, and flicked it into the cold evening air before turning back to the dilapidated hallway he was in. Something at the far end caught his eye, though.

A records room, perhaps something worth his time could be found there? He wandered in, the room lined floor to ceiling with filing cabinets, some torn from the walls, their contents flung all about. On a large and long table in the middle of the room where the pencil pushers likely did their tiresome work, sat a file marked in red which caught his eye. “ARREST RECORDS 1962-64” it practically screamed. He picked it up and flipped it open a few pages in.

Names, many many names. Accompanied by a brief description of their crime as well as a sentence. The document was rather thick, there could easily be over a thousand names in this record. Not to speak of other such records like this one. While idly scanning over it, something caused him to raise an eyebrow. “Valery Mikhailovich Sablin” it read “Rebellion against the state. Mutiny. Sedition. Sentence: Execution, firing squad” it stated bluntly.

With a dry laugh, and an overarm throw into a waste paper bin on the far side of the room, the document hit its mark with a dry thump. Making his way out, he struck a match and ignited another cigarette, meeting a pair of other officers who’d been lingering on the steps outside the building.

“Find anything interesting?” one of them asked disinterestedly, tobacco smoke clouding the air around them.

“Not really” Pavel replied, leaning on the doorframe. “Arrest and sentence records mostly, building's shot to shit. Would be more trouble than it's worth to get it back to working order” he continued, taking a long drag.

"might be able to recycle some materials from in there, wiring might still be good” his comrade suggested

Pavel tilted his head, considering this “I’ll get in contact with command, strip out anything useful and demolish the rest” he said with finality.

title: Cold Comfort
desc:
Igor had seen much in his time, born at the turn of the century and long before all the triumphs and tragedies that had ensued. He sat back in an old armchair while the fire crackled close by, leaning his head back as a feeling of nostalgia bit at him and he began to reminisce.

The first pictures to run through his mind were of the revolution which put the Bolsheviks in power. He was only a young man at the time, still living in Angarsk, so the revolution was well underway by the time news reached him. While he worked in a workshop at the time, all he had heard from friends and colleagues was of the revolution. Igor had been concerned that a new government would be no better than the old one.

The turmoil didn’t end there; various names vied for power, with Bukharin eventually coming out on top after Stalin's death. But that wasn’t the end of it. The Great Patriotic War would prove trying for everyone. Igor was shocked when news that Moscow had fallen filtered through. He had worked long and exhausting hours in a factory, likely inducing his current arthritis and it had all been for nothing. 

After that, the union which had seemed so very invincible shattered like a stone through a glass panel. Igor felt as though a trapdoor had opened beneath him, his mind spun with uncertainty as warlords sprung up across the broken nation. When his arthritis rendered him unable to work, he thankfully had family to move in with in the face of the whirlwinds of danger racing around him.

Despite bravado about scattering the Black League, the opposite had taken place, and now the League’s troops paraded through Irkutsk. But, if the Black League had picked up the pieces of a shattered nation, perhaps they could be strong enough to one day face the Reich? One could only hope. And these days, a single hope is enough to sustain you like a log in a fire.

title: Broken, But Not Shattered
desc:
Tank 237, was wandering around Siberian villages for nearly the whole afternoon, tasked with advanced reconnaissance to investigate rumors of Sablinite resistance following their government's capitulation. All of the villages they passed, from farming hamlets to town hubs were vacant, not a single soul was seen.  Abandoned buildings and town squares were devoid of life, with the occasional dead farm animal being feasted upon by wolves or crows. It was uncannily quiet, with the break in silence coming from the embers of a burning barn. Eventually, the crew of 237 stopped, their fuel had begun to run out. Luckily their logistics convoy was just a short distance behind and was coming to help refuel. The tank commander, Nevsky, climbed out and pulled out one of his cigars before lighting it. The fire from the stub tickling his cheekbones with comforting albeit brief warmth. He looked around, Nevsky assumed that the population fled in the face of their advance.

The fuel truck arrived and began refilling 237’s tank. It took a while but eventually  they were good to go, that was before a loud whistle and a house next to the tank exploded. Coming from the dense tree line in front of Tank 237, a rocket was fired, which was followed by a crescendo of bullets coming from the same direction. The small Black League convoy went into disarray. Everyone expected that the Sablinite army was scattered. They were wrong, it was there, and still had some fight in it. Finally, the main turret of the tank started to return fire. It was unclear how long the battle would last, but it was clear that blood would have to be shed.

options.name: The last followers of Lenin, raging against the dying of the light.

title: We Dared to hope
desc:
It was a new morning in Bada, Pavlov, the mayor, entered the town hall like any other day. The war with the black league passed them, and the fate of Sablin's Nation is unknown. But they were sure to have some rough months, maybe years from now on. Everyone greeted Pavlov as he moved with his briefcase up the stairs. The heating and lights were cut off the grid so they had to use generators. He eventually made it to the front of his office and opened the door. He placed his briefcase next to his desk as he laid back to catch his breath before a long day of work. He looked at his desk and saw an envelope. He opened it to see in big and red colors the word, NOTICE, reading it was the black league informing him about his town being on his territory now and that all orders are to be obeyed.

He breathed a sigh of relief. At least it didn't mean he would get shot. He eventually put the envelope to his side and began working. Yet, it wouldn't last. At around noon he heard something outside. After looking outside his window he saw a truck with a jeep in front of it parking in front of the town hall. He jumped out of his chair to investigate while passing all of his worried staff. As soon as he came outside an Officer stopped him with his palm pointing towards him.

"Under the Order of the Black League, you are to follow us."

Before he could respond one of the soldiers viciously grabbed both of his hands and placed them behind his head, while the others entered to look for his staff. He was led behind the Town Hall and placed on his knees. It was freezing. The officer lit up a cigarette behind him, after the officer saw him looking at him, he looked to see if the others were back, but they weren't, he was quick to place a cigarette in his mouth and lit it up while quickly returning to his position. After around 10 minutes the building was clear. His staff were all standing with their heads to the wall. They didn't say a word. Pavlov didn't say a word.

"PREPARE!" The Officer shouted as the men loaded their rifles.

"PRESENT!" The Staff were all panicking as Pavlov's secretary began crying. Yet he didn't panic, and he didn't cry, it was over, and the only way to accept it was by accepting what was going to happen. In his last moments, he thought of the officer who allowed him one last smoke.

title: Guilty after Guilty
desc:
The war was over. Whatever was left of the Amur government was in Black League hands. Igor woke up as always, washed his face, got his uniform, and left the barracks just to see that he had the honor of guarding a tribunal of blackshirts. After being driven in a truck with his comrades they arrived in front of the courthouse.  Igor stood straight with his rifle for around an hour, it was surprisingly warm inside the courtroom of all places. For at least half an hour he had seen at least four black shirts already guilty and sentenced to be shot. One of them didn't even have time to say anything. He didn't exactly understand why the court was even in session if every defendant was sentenced to death almost instantly. Perhaps for propaganda.

Two hours passed as more blackshirts were tried, all of them guilty and sentenced to death for treason. Yet one seemed to be more aggressive than his other ilk. He was trying to push the two guards carrying him away while shouting slurs and calling everyone "Jewish pigs". The two guards eventually forced him to sit down. The judge attempted to talk only for him to shout again at each attempt. A bailiff eventually got tired, pulled out his pistol, and without hesitation pulled the trigger behind his head. His head fell flat on the table and his body simply carried away shortly after. When the next defendant came in he was visibly disturbed by the fresh blood stain that tainted the wood covered desk, continuously looking behind him to check if he was going to meet his end on the chair as well.

It eventually ended after ten painful hours and Igor was soon on the truck heading back to his apartment. It was exhausting to just stand up, but the extra rations were worth it. While Igor was sitting on his bed his partner on the bed next to him asked how his day was. Igor simply looked at her and sighed.

title: The Merchants of Death, Outsold
desc:
In an unmarked room, in an unincorporated town, on the outskirts of Magadan, two men who weren't in Russia, along with one who most certainly was, sat down to have a meeting that never happened to discuss a state that never was.

"Alexander Lazarenko, I take it? We, uh, assure you that the United States of America had nothing to do with the deranged misadventures of that madman Werbell. Rather, we seek to ensure continued diplomatic ties with-"

"-You Americans are too damn sloppy."

"Excuse me?"

"You prop up an illegal puppet state on Russian soil, and upon its inevitable destruction act as if you had no hand in it. I know your game, and I have to say you're terrible at playing it."

"I apologize, Mr. Lazarenko, but there seems to have been a misunderstanding. The CIA would not back foreign dictators and warlords, nor would it operate against its allies. We simply ask for this to be cleaned up as nothing more than a minor, inconsequential stain on the clean surface of Russo-American cordiality, and for all CIA operatives and assets in the region to be allowed to be withdrawn. Surely a reasonable government such as yours would be more than amenable to such requests?"

For a moment, there was silence. Then, the sound of something sliding on the floor.

"Mr. Lazarenko you can't be serious-"

"Leave. And do not return. Let this generosity be the last act of its kind required."[Change Later]

options.name: And all that was left was a single, bloodied cap, lying still upon the floor.

title: Where Did We Go Wrong?
desc:
The dripping of water, the bad bed quality, the horrendous smell. Shukshin and Amet-Kahn were already beginning to get used to their new cell. Two small rusty beds with the worst mattress known to mankind, a sink, and a toilet that doesn't work. They were both still in their stained suits, as they were never even given a proper prisoner uniform. They were both staring at the ceiling until Amet-Kahn broke the silence.

"Where did we go wrong?"

Shukshin turned his head.

"Did we build too little? Did we prepare too little? Did we hope too little? Did we cause this?"

Shukshin would've normally said something to make his friend feel less guilty, but he was facing the reality, that he felt the same guilt as him. The unification wars were quite literally the worst time of his life. His winning against Pokryskin brought him hope, hope that things were finally going to get better. But when more and more reports came in detailing in mass detail how the Black League was seeing victory after victory. It gave him nightmares, and it seemed that the nightmares would become real. He was about to say something but then they heard a voice.

"Amet Khan Sultan, follow us please."

They both looked up to see men dressed all in black as if he was preparing for a funeral, one was an officer, and the two behind his shoulders were soldiers. Shukshin looked scared but Amet Khan didn't show a single expression, he simply got up and exited the cell, but before he left he turned to Shukshin one last time and said.

"I'll see you soon."

Shukshin sat in his cell alone, for hours, or so he assumed was hours, he lost track of time a long time ago. He was tired, but everything in him refused to rest. As things couldn't get worse. A shiver ran down his spine as the same officer came back..

options.name: [Change Later]"Let's get this over with, ‘Mr. President’."[Change Later]

title: Almost Painless
desc:
It was over, Novosibirsk has fallen. The Black League was advancing daily as the All-Siberian Army could do little to nothing at stopping their advance. What was left was no longer about defense but of evacuating. While the soldiers were fighting, many civilians were fleeing. The Siloviki, once the most influential men in the country, were reduced to a bunch of greedy businessmen getting on whatever that could fly to escape, either to their estates abroad in Japan or America or any country that would accept their money.

A prime example would be Artem Makarov, once sitting on the Sibir board of directors now running alongside his staff toward his private jet. All around the airfield civilians were climbing the fence to get in and on anything that had wings and wheels. Eventually, everyone was seated, the atmosphere tense, and everyone on the plane held their breath as the engines fired up to life. Artem looked out the window to see the turmoil, it was madness, civilians running as whatever security was left could do nothing other than be pushed down and trampled. The plane started moving as the runway began to be clogged with people. The pilot  turned to Artem. 

"Sir, it seems that the runway is blocked, we-"

"I don't care! Just take this plane off the ground!"

The pilot looked at him in disgust but held his tongue as a gunshot broke the silence. A security enforcer was shot as people were rushing towards the plane. The pilot pushed the throttle forward. People ducking mere meters from the wing. Artem looked down, as his heart sank seeing men in black uniforms entering the airport. The ground became smaller and smaller as he finally breathed a sigh of relief. The pilot mimicked Artem.

"Systems are nominal, we will be arriving in-"

All of a sudden, a loud  beeping emitted from the dashboard of the cockpit. Before anybody could say anything, the whole plane was engulfed in a fireball. It was almost a painless death. Five thousand feet below the fireball, a Black League officer simply said on his radio while standing next to his SAM launcher.

title: Ashes to Ashes
desc:
At 09:00 in the morning, Black League Troops entered the city of Bratsk situated on the Angara Sea. The City was previously bypassed by League troops on their advance. Reports showed that a sizable number of anarchist resistance has been reported, in response two infantry divisions have been ordered to move in from the north and west to secure the city. At around 10:00 the first serious combat began with orders to use artillery fire. League soldiers faced almost fanatical resistance from the local militia. At 10:30 the east of the city was fully secure with low to no resistance left. The Resistance in the West had seemingly no end with resistance to its fullest. At 12:00, a tank brigade was moved into the city.

At 13:30, North and South were cut into two, resistance was finally showing signs of slowing down. Already a quarter of the city was in rouble. Anarchists were using everything they had to fight, including bricks, rocks and even ramming cars into troops. At 14:50 with the help of the tank brigade, most of the fighting in the south of the city has ceased with all attention to the north now. Casualties, while not very high, were still a reason for concern for our troops. At 16:00 fighting in occupied areas ceased as our troops finished preparing for the final push. At 16:40 After a lengthy artillery bombardment, our troops entered the last pocket of resistance. Despite the long artillery bombardment, morale seemed to have not disappeared, and the resistance fighters still fought on. At 18:00, most of the fighting has ceased. The city is in absolute ruin, most of the civilians have fled or fought over what's left. Close to no resistance fighters surrendered. It is debatable if there is any worth in rebuilding the town or if it's better off just a burning memory.

options.name: Mother Anarchy embraces her sons for the last time.
